titleEn: Marvalu (Abutilon indicum) leaf paste for cough
communityOrTradition: Nicobarese traditional knowledge practitioners, Little Andaman Island, Andaman and Nicobar Islands

ingredients.name: Marvalu (leaf)
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 level teaspoon of freshly ground plant material

ingredients.name: Clean boiled and cooled water
ingredients.notes: 1 tablespoon of water to aid mortar maceration/grinding

steps: Measure 5 g of fresh, clean leaf of Marvalu (Abutilon indicum), wash thoroughly under potable running water, and chop into small pieces.
Grind the 5 g of leaf on a clean grinding stone or in a mortar with 15 ml of clean water until a smooth, uniform paste (kalka) is formed.
Measure out 1 level teaspoon (approx. 5 g) of the freshly ground paste and pair with a cup of lukewarm water.
Take 5 g (1 level teaspoon) of fresh herbal paste orally (once or twice daily for 3 days) for cough.
storage: Prepare fresh before each dose; do not keep wet herbal paste at room temperature for more than 4 hours.

traditionalUsage.typicalAdultAmount: 5 g (1 level teaspoon) of fresh herbal paste
traditionalUsage.typicalFrequency: once or twice daily for 3 days
traditionalUsage.traditionalTiming: Morning on an empty stomach or before meals

doshaEffect: Pacifies Kapha and Vata; supports clear respiratory channels (Pranavaha Srotas)

redFlagSymptoms: breathlessness or chest pain
coughing up blood
cough lasting more than 2-3 weeks
high fever (above 39 C) or fever lasting more than 3 days
noisy or difficult breathing in a child
stopAndSeeDoctorIf: These remedies are for adults. Do not give them to infants; for children, ask a clinician first.
If you are pregnant, breastfeeding, taking regular medicines, or have a long-term illness, ask a clinician before using this.
breathlessness or chest pain
coughing up blood
cough lasting more than 2-3 weeks
Do not use this to delay care for persistent cough, breathlessness or chest pain.

sources.citation: Chander MP, Vijayachari P. Ethnomedicinal knowledge among the tribes of the Little Andaman Island, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, India. Pharmacognosy Magazine. 2018;14(57 Suppl 2):S488-S493. doi:10.4103/pm.pm_585_17

evidenceNote: Traditional use documented in the Little Andaman Island tribal survey (Chander & Vijayachari, 2018). No clinical trials were located for this preparation.
folkloreNote: Preserved in the oral ethnobotanical heritage of Nicobarese traditional knowledge practitioners, Little Andaman Island, Andaman and Nicobar Islands (Andaman & Nicobar Islands), where locally gathered leaf of Marvalu (Abutilon indicum) is prepared at the household or community healer level as a customary primary-care remedy.
uncertaintyNotes: Primary ethnobotanical survey documents the plant part, indication, and traditional practice qualitatively; household preparation quantities and schedule reflect standard traditional Dravyaguna/folk practice. Botanical nomenclature verified against POWO.

titleEn: Olka (Annona reticulata) leaf maceration for skin injuries
communityOrTradition: Nicobarese traditional knowledge practitioners, Little Andaman Island, Andaman and Nicobar Islands

ingredients.name: Olka (leaf)
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 tablespoon of fresh plant material for maceration

ingredients.name: Clean boiled and cooled water
ingredients.notes: 1 tablespoon of water to aid mortar maceration/grinding

steps: Select 15 g of clean leaf of Olka (Annona reticulata) and wash thoroughly under running potable water to remove all surface dirt.
Crush and grind the 15 g of leaf in a clean stone mortar with 15 ml of clean water until a smooth, thick paste is formed.
Clean the affected skin area gently with potable water, pat dry with a clean cloth, and test a small dab of the preparation on intact skin first to check for sensitivity.

Apply 10-15 g of the prepared paste (sufficient to coat the affected area) externally over the affected site (once or twice daily for 3-5 days) for skin injuries, and rinse off gently with lukewarm water after 30-45 minutes.
storage: Grind fresh paste for each application; discard any unused wet paste after use.

traditionalUsage.typicalAdultAmount: 10-15 g of the prepared paste (sufficient to coat the affected area)
traditionalUsage.typicalFrequency: once or twice daily for 3-5 days

doshaEffect: Pacifies Pitta and Kapha; traditionally regarded as Vrana-ropana (wound-healing) and Tvachya (skin-soothing)

redFlagSymptoms: redness, swelling or pain that spreads
pus, red streaks, foul smell or fever with a wound
a wound that is deep, gaping, dirty or from a bite
a rash that spreads quickly or comes with fever
stopAndSeeDoctorIf: These remedies are for adults. Do not give them to infants; for children, ask a clinician first.
If you are pregnant, breastfeeding, taking regular medicines, or have a long-term illness, ask a clinician before using this.

titleEn: Tore-lu-lu (Drypetes assamica) leaves applied on an infected tooth
communityOrTradition: Onge traditional knowledge practitioners, Little Andaman Island, Andaman and Nicobar Islands
traditionalUses: traditionally applied on an infected tooth for dental caries

ingredients.name: Tore-lu-lu (leaf)
ingredients.notes: Approx. 4-6 fresh washed leaves or 1 small piece of root/shoot

steps: Measure 5 g of fresh, clean, tender leaf of Tore-lu-lu (Drypetes assamica) and wash thoroughly under clean running potable water.
Drain excess water and inspect the 5 g of leaf to ensure it is clean and intact.
Place in the mouth and chew slowly so the active plant juices mix thoroughly with saliva (or swallow with 100 ml of lukewarm water as traditionally practiced).
Take 5 g of fresh leaf (once or twice daily for 3 days) on an infected tooth for dental caries.
storage: Harvest and wash fresh immediately before use; do not store wet washed leaves for more than a few hours.

traditionalUsage.typicalAdultAmount: 5 g of fresh leaf
traditionalUsage.typicalFrequency: once or twice daily for 3 days

doshaEffect: Balances Kapha and Pitta in the oral cavity and throat (Kanthya and Mukharoga-hara)

drooling or inability to open the mouth
high fever with throat pain
mouth ulcers lasting more than 2 weeks
white patches in the mouth

communityOrTradition: Ethnic people of Krishna district, Andhra Pradesh

ingredients.name: Paala malli (root)

ingredients.name: Clean potable water

steps: Weigh 15 g of clean root of Paala malli (Aganosma dichotoma) along with 2 g of Black pepper (fruit), wash thoroughly under running potable water to remove any soil or surface debris, and chop or crush coarsely in a mortar.

Place the 15 g of crushed root and 2 g of Black pepper (fruit) into a clean stainless-steel or earthen pot with 200 ml of clean potable water, bring to a boil, and simmer gently over low heat for 10-15 minutes until the liquid reduces to about one-fourth to one-half of its original volume (approx. 50-75 ml).
Remove from heat, strain the decoction through a clean cotton cloth or fine mesh strainer into a cup, and allow it to cool to a comfortable lukewarm temperature.
Take 50 ml (approx. 3 tablespoons) of the warm strained decoction orally (Twice a day for three days) for fever.
storage: Consume fresh while warm; if needed, keep covered in a cool place and use within 12 hours.

titleEn: Kondacorintha (Acacia torta) stem for cough and bronchitis
communityOrTradition: Chenchu tribe, Yerragondapalem Mandal, Prakasam district, Andhra Pradesh
traditionalUses: traditionally used for cough and bronchitis

ingredients.name: Kondacorintha (stem)
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 tablespoon / small handful of clean, coarsely crushed plant material

ingredients.name: Clean potable water
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 cup of water for boiling decoction

steps: Weigh 15 g of clean stem of Kondacorintha (Senegalia torta), wash thoroughly under running potable water to remove any soil or surface debris, and chop or crush coarsely in a mortar.

Place the 15 g of crushed stem into a clean stainless-steel or earthen pot with 200 ml of clean potable water, bring to a boil, and simmer gently over low heat for 10-15 minutes until the liquid reduces to about one-fourth to one-half of its original volume (approx. 50-75 ml).
Remove from heat, strain the decoction through a clean cotton cloth or fine mesh strainer into a cup, and allow it to cool to a comfortable lukewarm temperature.
Take 50 ml (approx. 3 tablespoons) of the warm strained decoction orally (twice daily for 3-5 days) for cough and bronchitis.
storage: Consume fresh while warm; if needed, keep covered in a cool place and use within 12 hours.

titleEn: Vanavasa (Costus speciosus) rhizome for fever
communityOrTradition: Chenchu tribe, Yerragondapalem Mandal, Prakasam district, Andhra Pradesh

ingredients.name: Keukand (rhizome)
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 tablespoon / small handful of clean, coarsely crushed plant material

ingredients.name: Clean potable water
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 cup of water for boiling decoction

steps: Weigh 15 g of clean rhizome of Keukand (Cheilocostus speciosus), wash thoroughly under running potable water to remove any soil or surface debris, and chop or crush coarsely in a mortar.

Place the 15 g of crushed rhizome into a clean stainless-steel or earthen pot with 200 ml of clean potable water, bring to a boil, and simmer gently over low heat for 10-15 minutes until the liquid reduces to about one-fourth to one-half of its original volume (approx. 50-75 ml).
Remove from heat, strain the decoction through a clean cotton cloth or fine mesh strainer into a cup, and allow it to cool to a comfortable lukewarm temperature.
Take 50 ml (approx. 3 tablespoons) of the warm strained decoction orally (twice daily for 3-5 days) for fever.
storage: Consume fresh while warm; if needed, keep covered in a cool place and use within 12 hours.

titleEn: Veluthuru chettu (Dichrostachys cinerea) leaf for diarrhoea
communityOrTradition: Chenchu tribe, Yerragondapalem Mandal, Prakasam district, Andhra Pradesh

ingredients.name: Veluthuru chettu (leaf)
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 handful of fresh, washed plant material (yields ~10 ml expressed juice)

ingredients.name: Clean boiled and cooled water
ingredients.notes: 1 tablespoon of water to aid mortar maceration/grinding

steps: Harvest or select 15 g (approx. 1 handful) of fresh, healthy leaf of Veluthuru chettu (Dichrostachys cinerea), wash thoroughly under clean running water to remove dust, and drain excess moisture.
Transfer the 15 g of washed leaf to a clean stone mortar and pestle, add 15 ml of boiled and cooled water to moisten the tissue, and pound thoroughly into a wet macerated pulp.
Place the crushed pulp in a clean, folded muslin cloth and wring firmly into a small cup to collect approximately 10-15 ml (2-3 teaspoons) of fresh expressed juice/extract (swarasa).
Take 10 ml (2 teaspoons) of the freshly extracted liquid orally (twice daily for 3 days) for diarrhoea.
storage: Must be prepared fresh immediately before consumption; do not store expressed plant juice.

titleEn: Rangthangong (Dioscorea alata) boiled tuber for gastritis
communityOrTradition: Monpa traditional knowledge holders of Kalaktang, West Kameng district, Arunachal Pradesh

ingredients.name: Rangthangong (tuber)
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 tablespoon / small handful of clean, coarsely crushed plant material

ingredients.name: Clean potable water
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 cup of water for boiling decoction

steps: Weigh 15 g of clean tuber of Rangthangong (Dioscorea alata), wash thoroughly under running potable water to remove any soil or surface debris, and chop or crush coarsely in a mortar.

Place the 15 g of crushed tuber into a clean stainless-steel or earthen pot with 200 ml of clean potable water, bring to a boil, and simmer gently over low heat for 10-15 minutes until the liquid reduces to about one-fourth to one-half of its original volume (approx. 50-75 ml).
Remove from heat, strain the decoction through a clean cotton cloth or fine mesh strainer into a cup, and allow it to cool to a comfortable lukewarm temperature.
Take 50 ml (approx. 3 tablespoons) of the warm strained decoction orally (twice daily for 3-5 days) for gastritis.
storage: Consume fresh while warm; if needed, keep covered in a cool place and use within 12 hours.

titleEn: Kutki (Picrorhiza kurrooa) root for cold and fever

steps: Weigh 15 g of clean root of Kutki (Picrorhiza kurrooa), wash thoroughly under running potable water to remove any soil or surface debris, and chop or crush coarsely in a mortar.

Place the 15 g of crushed root into a clean stainless-steel or earthen pot with 200 ml of clean potable water, bring to a boil, and simmer gently over low heat for 10-15 minutes until the liquid reduces to about one-fourth to one-half of its original volume (approx. 50-75 ml).

Take 50 ml (approx. 3 tablespoons) of the warm strained decoction orally (twice daily for 3-5 days) for cold and fever.
storage: Consume fresh while warm; if needed, keep covered in a cool place and use within 12 hours.

titleEn: Xoru jhari (Acmella ciliata) leaf paste for tongue bumps

titleEn: Gufur barsiki (Justicia adhatoda) flower decoction for cough
communityOrTradition: Bodo traditional healers and knowledge holders of Baksa district, Assam

ingredients.name: Gufur barsiki (flower)
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 tablespoon / small handful of clean, coarsely crushed plant material

ingredients.name: Clean potable water
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 cup of water for boiling decoction

steps: Weigh 15 g of clean flower of Gufur barsiki (Justicia adhatoda), wash thoroughly under running potable water to remove any soil or surface debris, and chop or crush coarsely in a mortar.

Place the 15 g of crushed flower into a clean stainless-steel or earthen pot with 200 ml of clean potable water, bring to a boil, and simmer gently over low heat for 10-15 minutes until the liquid reduces to about one-fourth to one-half of its original volume (approx. 50-75 ml).
Remove from heat, strain the decoction through a clean cotton cloth or fine mesh strainer into a cup, and allow it to cool to a comfortable lukewarm temperature.
Take 50 ml (approx. 3 tablespoons) of the warm strained decoction orally (twice daily for 3-5 days) for cough.
storage: Consume fresh while warm; if needed, keep covered in a cool place and use within 12 hours.

titleEn: Athiyakol (Musa balbisiana) juice for diarrhoea
communityOrTradition: Bodo traditional healers and knowledge holders of Baksa district, Assam

ingredients.name: Athiyakol (fruit and young plant)
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 handful of fresh, washed plant material (yields ~10 ml expressed juice)

ingredients.name: Clean boiled and cooled water
ingredients.notes: 1 tablespoon of water to aid mortar maceration/grinding

steps: Harvest or select 15 g (approx. 1 handful) of fresh, healthy fruit and young plant of Athiyakol (Musa balbisiana), wash thoroughly under clean running water to remove dust, and drain excess moisture.
Transfer the 15 g of washed fruit and young plant to a clean stone mortar and pestle, add 15 ml of boiled and cooled water to moisten the tissue, and pound thoroughly into a wet macerated pulp.
Place the crushed pulp in a clean, folded muslin cloth and wring firmly into a small cup to collect approximately 10-15 ml (2-3 teaspoons) of fresh expressed juice/extract (swarasa).
Take 10 ml (2 teaspoons) of the freshly extracted liquid orally (twice daily for 3 days) for diarrhoea.
storage: Must be prepared fresh immediately before consumption; do not store expressed plant juice.

steps: Select 15 g of clean leaf of Sbai thai (Rungia parviflora) and wash thoroughly under running potable water to remove all surface dirt.
Crush and grind the 15 g of leaf in a clean stone mortar with 15 ml of clean water until a smooth, thick paste is formed.

titleEn: Khair (Senegalia catechu) bark decoction with milk for cold and cough
communityOrTradition: Medicine-men and residents of Aurangabad district, Magadh division, Bihar
traditionalUses: traditionally used for cold and cough

ingredients.name: Khair (bark)
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 tablespoon / small handful of clean, coarsely crushed plant material

ingredients.name: Warm milk
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1/2 cup warm milk

ingredients.name: Clean potable water
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 cup of water for boiling decoction

steps: Weigh 15 g of clean bark of Khair (Senegalia catechu), wash thoroughly under running potable water to remove any soil or surface debris, and chop or crush coarsely in a mortar. Also measure out 100 ml of Warm milk.

Place the 15 g of crushed bark into a clean stainless-steel or earthen pot with 200 ml of clean potable water, bring to a boil, and simmer gently over low heat for 10-15 minutes until the liquid reduces to about one-fourth to one-half of its original volume (approx. 50-75 ml).
Remove from heat, strain the hot decoction through a clean cotton cloth or fine mesh strainer into a cup, and stir in 100 ml of Warm milk while lukewarm.
Take 50 ml (approx. 3 tablespoons) of the warm strained decoction orally (twice daily for 3-5 days) for cold and cough.
storage: Consume fresh while warm; if needed, keep covered in a cool place and use within 12 hours.

traditionalUsage.typicalFrequency: twice daily for 3-5 days

titleEn: Sihora (Streblus asper) bark decoction for dysentery
communityOrTradition: Medicine-men and residents of Aurangabad district, Magadh division, Bihar
traditionalUses: traditionally used for dysentery and diarrhoea

ingredients.name: Seora (bark)
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 tablespoon / small handful of clean, coarsely crushed plant material

ingredients.name: Clean potable water
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 cup of water for boiling decoction

steps: Weigh 15 g of clean bark of Seora (Streblus asper), wash thoroughly under running potable water to remove any soil or surface debris, and chop or crush coarsely in a mortar.

Place the 15 g of crushed bark into a clean stainless-steel or earthen pot with 200 ml of clean potable water, bring to a boil, and simmer gently over low heat for 10-15 minutes until the liquid reduces to about one-fourth to one-half of its original volume (approx. 50-75 ml).

Take 50 ml (approx. 3 tablespoons) of the warm strained decoction orally (twice daily for 3-5 days) for dysentery and diarrhoea.
storage: Consume fresh while warm; if needed, keep covered in a cool place and use within 12 hours.

titleEn: Motha (Cyperus rotundus) root decoction for heartburn

ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 cup of water for boiling decoction

steps: Weigh 15 g of clean root of Motha (Cyperus rotundus), wash thoroughly under running potable water to remove any soil or surface debris, and chop or crush coarsely in a mortar.

Remove from heat, strain the decoction through a clean cotton cloth or fine mesh strainer into a cup, and allow it to cool to a comfortable lukewarm temperature.
Take 50 ml (approx. 3 tablespoons) of the warm strained decoction orally (once daily for 3 to 5 days for heartburn) for pyrosis (heartburn).
storage: Consume fresh while warm; if needed, keep covered in a cool place and use within 12 hours.

Transfer the 15 g of washed bark to a clean stone mortar and pestle, add 15 ml of boiled and cooled water to moisten the tissue, and pound thoroughly into a wet macerated pulp.
Place the crushed pulp in a clean, folded muslin cloth and wring firmly into a small cup to collect approximately 10-15 ml (2-3 teaspoons) of fresh expressed juice/extract (swarasa).
Take 10 ml (2 teaspoons) of the freshly extracted liquid orally (once daily) for cough.

titleEn: Chanbor (Ziziphus oenoplia) root crushed with water for cough

ingredients.name: Clean potable water
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 cup of water for boiling decoction

steps: Weigh 15 g of clean root of Chanbor (Ziziphus oenoplia), wash thoroughly under running potable water to remove any soil or surface debris, and chop or crush coarsely in a mortar.

Place the 15 g of crushed root into a clean stainless-steel or earthen pot with 200 ml of clean potable water, bring to a boil, and simmer gently over low heat for 10-15 minutes until the liquid reduces to about one-fourth to one-half of its original volume (approx. 50-75 ml).
Remove from heat, strain the decoction through a clean cotton cloth or fine mesh strainer into a cup, and allow it to cool to a comfortable lukewarm temperature.
Take 50 ml (approx. 3 tablespoons) of the warm strained decoction orally (twice daily for 3-5 days) for cough.
storage: Consume fresh while warm; if needed, keep covered in a cool place and use within 12 hours.

titleEn: Til (Sesamum indicum) aerial parts decoction for constipation
communityOrTradition: Traditional healers and local informants of the Delhi Ridge (Aravalli) area, National Capital Territory of Delhi

ingredients.name: Til (aerial parts and roots)
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 tablespoon / small handful of clean, coarsely crushed plant material

ingredients.name: Clean potable water
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 cup of water for boiling decoction

steps: Weigh 15 g of clean aerial parts and roots of Til (Sesamum indicum), wash thoroughly under running potable water to remove any soil or surface debris, and chop or crush coarsely in a mortar.

Place the 15 g of crushed aerial parts and roots into a clean stainless-steel or earthen pot with 200 ml of clean potable water, bring to a boil, and simmer gently over low heat for 10-15 minutes until the liquid reduces to about one-fourth to one-half of its original volume (approx. 50-75 ml).
Remove from heat, strain the decoction through a clean cotton cloth or fine mesh strainer into a cup, and allow it to cool to a comfortable lukewarm temperature.
Take 50 ml (approx. 3 tablespoons) of the warm strained decoction orally (twice daily for 3-5 days) for constipation.
storage: Consume fresh while warm; if needed, keep covered in a cool place and use within 12 hours.

titleEn: Sotsal (Malva sylvestris) seeds boiled in sharbat for cough
communityOrTradition: Hakims and local people of the Kashmir Himalaya, Jammu and Kashmir

ingredients.name: Sotsal (Malva sylvestris) seeds
ingredients.notes: Approx. 2 teaspoons mucilaginous mallow seeds

ingredients.name: Natural sugar / mishri
ingredients.notes: 1 tablespoon for traditional sharbat syrup

ingredients.name: Clean potable water
ingredients.notes: 1 cup of water

steps: Measure 10 g (2 teaspoons) of clean Sotsal (Malva sylvestris) seeds and rinse briefly in a fine strainer.

Place the 10 g of seeds and 15 g (1 tablespoon) of natural sugar (mishri) in a saucepan with 200 ml of water and simmer gently over low heat for 8-10 minutes until a soothing, slightly mucilaginous sharbat forms.
Strain the warm sharbat through a clean muslin cloth into a cup.
Sip 100-150 ml of the warm sharbat orally once or twice daily for 3-5 days to soothe dry cough and throat irritation.
storage: Consume fresh while warm; refrigerate any remainder and use within 24 hours.

traditionalUsage.typicalAdultAmount: 100-150 ml warm herbal sharbat
traditionalUsage.typicalFrequency: Once or twice daily for 3-5 days

doshaEffect: Pacifies Kapha and Vata; supports clear respiratory channels (Pranavaha Srotas)

titleEn: Bunafsha (Viola odorata) flowers with sugar in kahwa for cough and hoarseness
communityOrTradition: Hakims and local people of the Kashmir Himalaya, Jammu and Kashmir
traditionalUses: traditionally used for cough, hoarseness of voice and sore throat

ingredients.name: Bunafsha (Viola odorata) fresh flowers
ingredients.notes: Crushed with sugar to prepare traditional Kashmiri khambir (gulkand-style conserve)

ingredients.name: Natural cane sugar / mishri
ingredients.notes: Mixed 1:2 with flowers for khambir fermentation

steps: Crush 5 g of clean Bunafsha (Viola odorata) flowers with 10 g of natural sugar in a mortar (traditionally aged in a clean glass jar in sunlight for 5-7 days to form fermented khambir conserve).
Prepare 150 ml (1 cup) of hot Kashmiri kahwa (or freshly boiled water) in a cup.
Stir 5-10 g (1-2 teaspoons) of the Bunafsha-sugar khambir preparation into the 150 ml of hot kahwa and let steep for 2-3 minutes.
Sip the warm infusion slowly once or twice daily for 3-5 days to relieve cough, hoarseness of voice, and sore throat.
storage: The sugar-preserved khambir keeps in a clean airtight glass jar for up to 3 months; drink the prepared kahwa fresh while warm.

titleEn: Kawdach (Berberis lycium) soft root peelings in sugary water for indigestion and constipation
communityOrTradition: Hakims and local people of the Kashmir Himalaya, Jammu and Kashmir
traditionalUses: traditionally used to relieve indigestion and constipation

ingredients.name: Kawdach (soft root peelings)
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 tablespoon / small handful of clean, coarsely crushed plant material

ingredients.name: Clean potable water
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 cup of water for boiling decoction

steps: Weigh 15 g of clean soft root peelings of Kawdach (Berberis lycium), wash thoroughly under running potable water to remove any soil or surface debris, and chop or crush coarsely in a mortar.

Place the 15 g of crushed soft root peelings into a clean stainless-steel or earthen pot with 200 ml of clean potable water, bring to a boil, and simmer gently over low heat for 10-15 minutes until the liquid reduces to about one-fourth to one-half of its original volume (approx. 50-75 ml).
Remove from heat, strain the decoction through a clean cotton cloth or fine mesh strainer into a cup, and allow it to cool to a comfortable lukewarm temperature.
Take 50 ml (approx. 3 tablespoons) of the warm strained decoction orally (twice daily for 3-5 days) to relieve indigestion and constipation.
storage: Consume fresh while warm; if needed, keep covered in a cool place and use within 12 hours.

traditionalUsage.typicalAdultAmount: 50 ml (approx. 3 tablespoons) of the warm strained decoction
traditionalUsage.typicalFrequency: twice daily for 3-5 days

doshaEffect: Balances Pachaka Pitta and Samana Vata; supports digestive fire (Agni) and gut motility (Annavaha Srotas)

titleEn: Pudina (Mentha arvensis) aerial powder with dilute curd (lassi) for sore throat
communityOrTradition: Hakims and local people of the Kashmir Himalaya, Jammu and Kashmir

ingredients.name: Pudina (aerial portion)
ingredients.notes: Approx. 0.5-1 level teaspoon of shade-dried, finely sieved powder (churna)

ingredients.name: Fresh curd (yoghurt)
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1/2 cup fresh unsoured curd

steps: Collect clean, mature aerial portion of Pudina (Mentha arvensis), dry thoroughly in the shade until completely moisture-free, and grind in a dry mortar or mill; sieve through a fine mesh to measure out 3 g of fine powder (churna).
Measure out 100 ml of Fresh curd (yoghurt) as the traditional vehicle (anupana) in a clean cup or bowl.
Mix the 3 g of fine herbal powder thoroughly into 100 ml of Fresh curd (yoghurt) until uniform.
Take 3 g (approx. 0.5-1 level teaspoon) of herbal powder in vehicle orally (once or twice daily for 3-7 days) for sore throat.
storage: Store the dry sieved powder in a clean, airtight glass jar away from moisture and sunlight for up to 2 months.

titleEn: Danthiveer (Salix wallichiana) leaf decoction wash for feet and legs during fever
communityOrTradition: Hakims and local people of the Kashmir Himalaya, Jammu and Kashmir
traditionalUses: traditionally used to wash the feet and lower legs to relieve fever and general body pain

ingredients.name: Danthiveer (leaf)
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 generous handful of clean plant material for boiling

ingredients.name: Clean potable water
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 cup of water for boiling decoction

steps: Weigh 20 g of clean leaf of Danthiveer (Salix wallichiana), wash thoroughly under running water, and crush or chop coarsely.
Place the 20 g of prepared plant material in a pot with 200 ml of clean water and boil gently for 10-15 minutes to extract the active constituents.
Strain the boiled liquid through a clean cloth and dilute into a bucket of warm bath water (or cool to a skin-safe lukewarm temperature for a local wash).
Wash or bathe the affected area with 250-500 ml of strained herbal decoction (once daily for 3-5 days) to wash the feet and lower legs to relieve fever and general body pain.
storage: Prepare fresh warm decoction for each wash, gargle, or fomentation; do not store beyond 12 hours.

titleEn: Archu (Rheum emodi) rhizome powder paste for wounds and winter frost injury
communityOrTradition: Hakims and local people of the Kashmir Himalaya, Jammu and Kashmir
traditionalUses: traditionally used for wounds of the body and winter frost of external body parts

ingredients.name: Archu (rhizome)
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 tablespoon of fresh, washed plant material for grinding into paste

ingredients.name: Clean boiled and cooled water
ingredients.notes: 1 tablespoon of water to aid mortar maceration/grinding

steps: Select 15 g of clean rhizome of Archu (Rheum emodi) and wash thoroughly under running potable water to remove all surface dirt.
Crush and grind the 15 g of rhizome in a clean stone mortar with 15 ml of clean water until a smooth, thick paste is formed.
Clean the affected skin area gently with potable water, pat dry with a clean cloth, and test a small dab of the preparation on intact skin first to check for sensitivity.

Apply 10-15 g of the prepared paste (sufficient to coat the affected area) externally over the affected site (once or twice daily for 3-5 days) for wounds of the body and winter frost of external body parts, and rinse off gently with lukewarm water after 30-45 minutes.
storage: Grind fresh paste for each application; discard any unused wet paste after use.

traditionalUsage.typicalFrequency: once or twice daily for 3-5 days

titleEn: Doddapatre thambuli (yoghurt curry with Indian borage)
communityOrTradition: Coastal Karnataka (Mangalore region) home cooking
traditionalUses: traditionally eaten with rice as a cooling everyday dish

ingredients.name: Doddapatre (Plectranthus amboinicus) fresh leaves
ingredients.notes: Approx. 10-12 thick aromatic leaves, washed and chopped

ingredients.name: Fresh unsoured curd (yoghurt)
ingredients.notes: 1 cup, whisked until smooth

ingredients.name: Freshly grated coconut
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1/4 cup grated coconut

ingredients.name: Cow ghee
ingredients.notes: 1 teaspoon, divided for roasting and tempering

ingredients.name: Cumin (Cuminum cyminum) seeds
ingredients.notes: 0.5 teaspoon for roasting with leaves

ingredients.name: Black pepper (Piper nigrum) corns
ingredients.notes: 5-6 whole black peppercorns

ingredients.name: Mustard (Brassica nigra) seeds
ingredients.notes: 0.5 teaspoon for tempering

ingredients.name: Fresh curry leaves (Murraya koenigii)
ingredients.notes: 6-8 fresh leaves for tempering

ingredients.name: Asafoetida (Ferula assa-foetida)
ingredients.notes: 1 pinch for tempering

ingredients.name: Rock salt (saindhava lavana)
ingredients.notes: 0.5 teaspoon to taste

steps: Heat 2.5 ml (0.5 teaspoon) of cow ghee in a small pan, add 2.5 g (0.5 teaspoon) of cumin seeds and 1 g (5-6) of black peppercorns, and roast until aromatic, then add 15 g (10-12) of washed Doddapatre leaves and saute for 1-2 minutes until wilted.
Transfer the cooled roasted leaves and spices to a blender or stone grinder, add 30 g (1/4 cup) of freshly grated coconut and 50 ml of water, and grind into a smooth, fine paste.
Whisk the ground coconut-herb paste into 200 ml (1 cup) of fresh unsoured curd along with 2.5 g (0.5 teaspoon) of rock salt.

Heat the remaining 2.5 ml (0.5 teaspoon) of ghee in a tempering ladle, splutter 2.5 g of mustard seeds, 2 g (6-8) of curry leaves, and 0.25 g (1 pinch) of asafoetida, pour over the thambuli, and serve with warm rice at midday.
storage: Refrigerate and consume within 24 hours; do not keep unpasteurised curd dishes at room temperature.

titleEn: Dasavala (hibiscus) flower in coconut oil for mouth ulcers
communityOrTradition: Traditional healers and communities of Uttara Kannada district

ingredients.name: Jaba (flower)
ingredients.notes: Clean plant material for infusing into base oil

ingredients.name: Coconut oil
ingredients.notes: 1 tablespoon of traditional carrier oil

steps: Weigh 15 g of clean flower of Jaba (Hibiscus rosa-sinensis), wash if fresh, and crush or grind into a coarse paste/powder.

Combine the 15 g of prepared flower with 15 ml of coconut oil in a heavy-bottomed pan and simmer gently over very low heat for 10-15 minutes until watery moisture evaporates and the active herbal principles infuse into the oil.

steps: Weigh 15 g of clean leaf of Indian coral tree (Erythrina variegata), wash thoroughly under running potable water to remove any soil or surface debris, and chop or crush coarsely in a mortar.

Place the 15 g of crushed leaf into a clean stainless-steel or earthen pot with 200 ml of clean potable water, bring to a boil, and simmer gently over low heat for 10-15 minutes until the liquid reduces to about one-fourth to one-half of its original volume (approx. 50-75 ml).
Remove from heat, strain the decoction through a clean cotton cloth or fine mesh strainer into a cup, and allow it to cool to a comfortable lukewarm temperature.
Take 50 ml (approx. 3 tablespoons) of the warm strained decoction orally (twice daily for 3-5 days) for arthritis.
storage: Consume fresh while warm; if needed, keep covered in a cool place and use within 12 hours.

titleEn: Adalodakam (malabar nut) leaf juice for cough
communityOrTradition: Mullu kuruma tribe, Wayanad district

ingredients.name: Malabar nut (leaf and root)
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 handful of fresh, washed plant material (yields ~10 ml expressed juice)

ingredients.name: Clean boiled and cooled water
ingredients.notes: 1 tablespoon of water to aid mortar maceration/grinding

steps: Harvest or select 15 g (approx. 1 handful) of fresh, healthy leaf and root of Malabar nut (Justicia adhatoda), wash thoroughly under clean running water to remove dust, and drain excess moisture.
Transfer the 15 g of washed leaf and root to a clean stone mortar and pestle, add 15 ml of boiled and cooled water to moisten the tissue, and pound thoroughly into a wet macerated pulp.
Place the crushed pulp in a clean, folded muslin cloth and wring firmly into a small cup to collect approximately 10-15 ml (2-3 teaspoons) of fresh expressed juice/extract (swarasa).
Take 10 ml (2 teaspoons) of the freshly extracted liquid orally (twice daily for 3 days) for cough.

titleEn: Tulsi leaf steam inhalation for cold, cough and fever
communityOrTradition: Mullu kuruma tribe, Wayanad district
traditionalUses: traditionally used for cold, cough and mild fever

ingredients.name: Holy basil (leaf)
ingredients.notes: Approx. 2 handfuls of fresh aromatic plant material for boiling

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 cup of clean potable water

steps: Weigh 30 g of clean leaf of Holy basil (Ocimum tenuiflorum), wash thoroughly under running water, and crush or chop coarsely.
Place the 30 g of prepared plant material in a pot with 200 ml of clean water and boil gently for 10-15 minutes to extract the active constituents.

Remove the pot from direct flame and place on a stable trivet at a safe distance (at least 30 cm from the face) to prevent steam burns, or dip a clean cotton cloth in the warm liquid and wring out excess water.
Apply 5-10 minutes of gentle steam inhalation or warm cloth fomentation (once or twice daily for 3 days) for cold, cough and mild fever.
storage: Prepare fresh warm decoction for each wash, gargle, or fomentation; do not store beyond 12 hours.

titleEn: Karkidaka kanji (monsoon medicinal rice gruel)
communityOrTradition: Karkidakam (Varsha ritu) tradition across Kerala

traditionally taken to support digestion during the rainy season

ingredients.name: Shashtika shali (Oryza sativa / Njavara rice)
ingredients.notes: Traditional red medicinal rice, washed thoroughly

ingredients.name: Mudga (Vigna radiata / green gram)
ingredients.notes: Whole or split green gram

ingredients.name: Balamoola churna (Sida cordifolia root powder)

ingredients.notes: Garden cress seeds

ingredients.name: Jeeraka (Cuminum cyminum) seeds

ingredients.notes: Freshly extracted first coconut milk

ingredients.name: Clean potable water
ingredients.notes: For decoction and cooking the rice gruel

ingredients.name: Palm jaggery or cane jaggery
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 tablespoon grated jaggery

ingredients.name: Saindhava lavana (rock salt)
ingredients.notes: 0.5 teaspoon to taste

steps: Boil 10 g of Balamoola churna in 500 ml of water for 10 minutes and strain through a clean cloth to obtain the herbal decoction base.
Wash 100 g of Shashtika shali (Njavara rice) and 10 g of Mudga (green gram), add them to the boiling Balamoola decoction, and cook over medium-low heat.
Add 10 g of Jeeraka (cumin), 10 g of Methika (fenugreek), 10 g of Chandrashoora (garden cress), and 5 g of Panchakola churna to the simmering porridge and cook until the grains are soft.
Stir in 15 ml (1 tablespoon) of fresh Dashapushpa swarasa, 100 ml of thick coconut milk, 20 g of jaggery, and 2.5 g of rock salt, simmer gently for 2 minutes, and serve warm once daily.
storage: Consume fresh while warm; refrigerate any leftovers promptly and reheat thoroughly within 24 hours.

titleEn: Chukku kappi (dry ginger herbal coffee)
communityOrTradition: Kerala household remedy, described by an Ayurvedic doctor
traditionalUses: traditionally taken as a warming drink during cold and cough

ingredients.name: Chukku (Zingiber officinale) dried ginger powder
ingredients.notes: 1 level teaspoon dry ginger powder

ingredients.name: Roasted coffee powder
ingredients.notes: 1 level teaspoon traditional coffee powder

ingredients.name: Kurumulaku (Piper nigrum) crushed black pepper
ingredients.notes: 0.5 teaspoon coarsely crushed peppercorns

ingredients.name: Malli (Coriandrum sativum) crushed coriander seeds
ingredients.notes: 1 teaspoon lightly crushed coriander seeds

ingredients.name: Jeerakam (Cuminum cyminum) cumin seeds
ingredients.notes: 0.5 teaspoon cumin seeds

ingredients.name: Uluva (Trigonella foenum-graecum) fenugreek seeds
ingredients.notes: 0.25 teaspoon fenugreek seeds

ingredients.name: Tulasi (Ocimum tenuiflorum) fresh leaves
ingredients.notes: 6-8 fresh washed holy basil leaves

ingredients.name: Karupatti (palm jaggery)
ingredients.notes: 1 tablespoon crushed palm jaggery to taste

ingredients.name: Clean potable water
ingredients.notes: 1 tall cup of water

steps: Crush 3 g of coriander seeds, 1.5 g of black peppercorns, 1.5 g of cumin seeds, and 1 g of fenugreek seeds coarsely in a mortar.
Bring 250 ml of water to a rolling boil in a saucepan, add the crushed spices along with 3 g (1 teaspoon) of dried ginger (chukku) powder, 2 g (6-8) of fresh tulsi leaves, and 15 g of palm jaggery.
Boil the mixture over low-to-medium heat for 8-10 minutes so the spices infuse fully, then stir in 3 g (1 teaspoon) of coffee powder and simmer for 1 more minute.
Remove from heat, let settle for 1 minute, strain through a fine mesh strainer, and drink 150-200 ml warm in the morning or evening.
storage: Best consumed fresh while warm; do not store brewed herbal coffee for more than 6-8 hours.

Transfer the 15 g of washed whole plant to a clean stone mortar and pestle, add 15 ml of boiled and cooled water to moisten the tissue, and pound thoroughly into a wet macerated pulp.

titleEn: Aanachukku (Hedychium flavescens) rhizome decoction for diarrhoea
communityOrTradition: Kaadar tribe, Sholayar forest, Thrissur district

ingredients.name: Aanachukku (rhizome and leaf)
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 tablespoon / small handful of clean, coarsely crushed plant material

ingredients.name: Clean potable water
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 cup of water for boiling decoction

steps: Weigh 15 g of clean rhizome and leaf of Aanachukku (Hedychium flavescens), wash thoroughly under running potable water to remove any soil or surface debris, and chop or crush coarsely in a mortar.

Place the 15 g of crushed rhizome and leaf into a clean stainless-steel or earthen pot with 200 ml of clean potable water, bring to a boil, and simmer gently over low heat for 10-15 minutes until the liquid reduces to about one-fourth to one-half of its original volume (approx. 50-75 ml).
Remove from heat, strain the decoction through a clean cotton cloth or fine mesh strainer into a cup, and allow it to cool to a comfortable lukewarm temperature.
Take 50 ml (approx. 3 tablespoons) of the warm strained decoction orally (twice daily for 3-5 days) for diarrhoea.
storage: Consume fresh while warm; if needed, keep covered in a cool place and use within 12 hours.

titleEn: Vathamkolli (Justicia gendarussa) leaf bath for rheumatism

traditionalUses: traditionally used as a warm leaf bath for rheumatism

ingredients.name: Vathamkolli (leaf)

steps: Weigh 30 g of clean leaf of Vathamkolli (Justicia gendarussa), wash thoroughly under running water, and crush or chop coarsely.
Place the 30 g of prepared plant material in a pot with 200 ml of clean water and boil gently for 10-15 minutes to extract the active constituents.

communityOrTradition: Native islanders of Lakshadweep (surveyed across all inhabited islands)

ingredients.name: Fappul (leaf)
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 handful of fresh, washed plant material (yields ~10 ml expressed juice)

ingredients.name: Clean boiled and cooled water

steps: Harvest or select 15 g (approx. 1 handful) of fresh, healthy leaf of Fappul (Launaea sarmentosa), wash thoroughly under clean running water to remove dust, and drain excess moisture.
Transfer the 15 g of washed leaf to a clean stone mortar and pestle, add 15 ml of boiled and cooled water to moisten the tissue, and pound thoroughly into a wet macerated pulp.
Place the crushed pulp in a clean, folded muslin cloth and wring firmly into a small cup to collect approximately 10-15 ml (2-3 teaspoons) of fresh expressed juice/extract (swarasa).
Take 10 ml (2 teaspoons) of the freshly extracted liquid orally (twice daily for 3 days) for gas trouble.

titleEn: Sholom (Suriana maritima) leaf and bark bath for arthritis

ingredients.name: Clean water
ingredients.notes: 2 cups of water for boiling herbal wash/steam

steps: Weigh 50 g of clean leaf and bark of Sholom (Suriana maritima), wash thoroughly under running water, and crush or chop coarsely.
Place the 50 g of prepared plant material in a pot with 500 ml of clean water and boil gently for 10-15 minutes to extract the active constituents.
Strain the boiled liquid through a clean cloth and dilute into a bucket of warm bath water (or cool to a skin-safe lukewarm temperature for a local wash).
Wash or bathe the affected area with 250-500 ml of strained herbal decoction (once daily for 3-5 days) in a bath for arthritis and skin diseases.

communityOrTradition: Native islanders of Lakshadweep (surveyed across all inhabited islands)
traditionalUses: traditionally used for gas trouble mediated stomach pain and rheumatism

ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 tablespoon / small handful of clean, coarsely crushed plant material

ingredients.name: Clean potable water
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 cup of water for boiling decoction

steps: Weigh 15 g of clean root of Foybettila (Tylophora indica), wash thoroughly under running potable water to remove any soil or surface debris, and chop or crush coarsely in a mortar.

Take 50 ml (approx. 3 tablespoons) of the warm strained decoction orally (twice daily for 3-5 days) for gas trouble mediated stomach pain and rheumatism.

titleEn: Kala Dhawda (Anogeissus pendula) bark decoction for cough
communityOrTradition: Tribal communities (mainly Korku, with Gond, Bhil, Bhilala, Naik, Mankar and Nihal) of East Nimar, Madhya Pradesh

ingredients.name: Kala Dhawda (bark)
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 tablespoon / small handful of clean, coarsely crushed plant material

ingredients.name: Clean potable water
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 cup of water for boiling decoction

steps: Weigh 15 g of clean bark of Kala Dhawda (Anogeissus pendula), wash thoroughly under running potable water to remove any soil or surface debris, and chop or crush coarsely in a mortar.

Place the 15 g of crushed bark into a clean stainless-steel or earthen pot with 200 ml of clean potable water, bring to a boil, and simmer gently over low heat for 10-15 minutes until the liquid reduces to about one-fourth to one-half of its original volume (approx. 50-75 ml).
Remove from heat, strain the decoction through a clean cotton cloth or fine mesh strainer into a cup, and allow it to cool to a comfortable lukewarm temperature.
Take 50 ml (approx. 3 tablespoons) of the warm strained decoction orally (twice daily for 3-5 days) for cough.
storage: Consume fresh while warm; if needed, keep covered in a cool place and use within 12 hours.

Take 50 ml (approx. 3 tablespoons) of the warm strained decoction orally (Once a day for one to two days) for dysentery with stomachache.

titleEn: Jahynwet (Prunella vulgaris) tender leaf paste for cuts and wounds
communityOrTradition: Khasi traditional practitioners and village folks of the Khasi hills, Meghalaya
traditionalUses: traditionally applied on cuts and wounds

ingredients.name: Kulwauth (tender leaf)
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 tablespoon of fresh, washed plant material for grinding into paste

ingredients.name: Clean boiled and cooled water
ingredients.notes: 1 tablespoon of water to aid mortar maceration/grinding

steps: Select 15 g of clean tender leaf of Kulwauth (Prunella vulgaris) and wash thoroughly under running potable water to remove all surface dirt.
Crush and grind the 15 g of tender leaf in a clean stone mortar with 15 ml of clean water until a smooth, thick paste is formed.
Clean the affected skin area gently with potable water, pat dry with a clean cloth, and test a small dab of the preparation on intact skin first to check for sensitivity.

Apply 10-15 g of the prepared paste (sufficient to coat the affected area) externally over the affected site (once or twice daily for 3-5 days) on cuts and wounds, and rinse off gently with lukewarm water after 30-45 minutes.
storage: Grind fresh paste for each application; discard any unused wet paste after use.

traditionalUsage.typicalAdultAmount: 10-15 g of the prepared paste (sufficient to coat the affected area)
traditionalUsage.typicalFrequency: once or twice daily for 3-5 days

doshaEffect: Pacifies Pitta and Kapha; traditionally regarded as Vrana-ropana (wound-healing) and Tvachya (skin-soothing)

a wound that is deep, gaping, dirty or from a bite

ingredients.name: Sohlia (stem bark)
ingredients.notes: Approx. 0.5-1 level teaspoon of shade-dried, finely sieved powder (churna)

ingredients.name: Lukewarm potable water
ingredients.notes: 1 teacup of water for steeping/mixing

steps: Collect clean, mature stem bark of Sohlia (Myrica nagi), dry thoroughly in the shade until completely moisture-free, and grind in a dry mortar or mill; sieve through a fine mesh to measure out 3 g of fine powder (churna).
Measure 150 ml of lukewarm potable water into a clean glass.
Stir the 3 g of fine herbal powder into the 150 ml of lukewarm water until evenly dispersed.
Take 3 g (approx. 0.5-1 level teaspoon) of herbal powder in vehicle orally (once or twice daily for 3-7 days) for dysentery.

steps: Collect clean, mature root of Thangtung (Arenga pinnata), dry thoroughly in the shade until completely moisture-free, and grind in a dry mortar or mill; sieve through a fine mesh to measure out 3 g of fine powder (churna).

Take 3 g (approx. 0.5-1 level teaspoon) of herbal powder in vehicle orally (once or twice daily for 3-7 days) for bronchitis.

titleEn: Hnah Kawi (Polygonatum cirrhifolium) root decoction for bronchitis
communityOrTradition: Lushai, Bru, Chakma, Lai, Bawm, Mara and Hmar communities of Mizoram

ingredients.name: Hnah Kawi (root)
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 tablespoon / small handful of clean, coarsely crushed plant material

ingredients.name: Clean potable water
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 cup of water for boiling decoction

steps: Weigh 15 g of clean root of Hnah Kawi (Polygonatum cirrhifolium), wash thoroughly under running potable water to remove any soil or surface debris, and chop or crush coarsely in a mortar.

Place the 15 g of crushed root into a clean stainless-steel or earthen pot with 200 ml of clean potable water, bring to a boil, and simmer gently over low heat for 10-15 minutes until the liquid reduces to about one-fourth to one-half of its original volume (approx. 50-75 ml).
Remove from heat, strain the decoction through a clean cotton cloth or fine mesh strainer into a cup, and allow it to cool to a comfortable lukewarm temperature.
Take 50 ml (approx. 3 tablespoons) of the warm strained decoction orally (twice daily for 3-5 days) for bronchitis.
storage: Consume fresh while warm; if needed, keep covered in a cool place and use within 12 hours.

communityOrTradition: Lushai, Bru, Chakma, Lai, Bawm, Mara and Hmar communities of Mizoram

ingredients.name: Sisu (fruit)
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 handful of fresh, washed plant material (yields ~10 ml expressed juice)

ingredients.name: Clean boiled and cooled water
ingredients.notes: 1 tablespoon of water to aid mortar maceration/grinding

steps: Harvest or select 15 g (approx. 1 handful) of fresh, healthy fruit of Sisu (Citrus aurantium), wash thoroughly under clean running water to remove dust, and drain excess moisture.
Transfer the 15 g of washed fruit to a clean stone mortar and pestle, add 15 ml of boiled and cooled water to moisten the tissue, and pound thoroughly into a wet macerated pulp.
Place the crushed pulp in a clean, folded muslin cloth and wring firmly into a small cup to collect approximately 10-15 ml (2-3 teaspoons) of fresh expressed juice/extract (swarasa).
Take 10 ml (2 teaspoons) of the freshly extracted liquid orally (twice daily for 3 days) for stomachache.
storage: Must be prepared fresh immediately before consumption; do not store expressed plant juice.

allergens: Citrus may worsen acidity in some people

steps: Weigh 15 g of clean root of Moosli (Curculigo orchioides), wash thoroughly under running potable water to remove any soil or surface debris, and chop or crush coarsely in a mortar. Also measure out 100 ml of Fresh curd (yoghurt).

Remove from heat, strain the hot decoction through a clean cotton cloth or fine mesh strainer into a cup, and stir in 100 ml of Fresh curd (yoghurt) while lukewarm.

communityOrTradition: Lepcha tribe of Dzongu valley, North Sikkim

steps: Weigh 15 g of clean whole plant of Bedina (Mussaenda frondosa), wash thoroughly under running potable water to remove any soil or surface debris, and chop or crush coarsely in a mortar.

Remove from heat, strain the decoction through a clean cotton cloth or fine mesh strainer into a cup, and allow it to cool to a comfortable lukewarm temperature.
Take 50 ml (approx. 3 tablespoons) of the warm strained decoction orally (twice daily for 3-5 days) for cough.

titleEn: Mudakkatthan (Cardiospermum halicacabum) decoction with ginger and cumin for rheumatism
communityOrTradition: Malasar tribes, Coimbatore district

ingredients.name: Balloon vine (whole plant)
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 tablespoon / small handful of clean, coarsely crushed plant material

ingredients.name: Dried ginger rhizome
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 teaspoon co-ingredient

ingredients.name: Cumin seeds
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 teaspoon co-ingredient

ingredients.name: Clean potable water
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 cup of water for boiling decoction

steps: Weigh 15 g of clean whole plant of Balloon vine (Cardiospermum halicacabum) along with 5 g of Dried ginger rhizome, 5 g of Cumin seeds, wash thoroughly under running potable water to remove any soil or surface debris, and chop or crush coarsely in a mortar.

Place the 15 g of crushed whole plant and 5 g of Dried ginger rhizome, 5 g of Cumin seeds into a clean stainless-steel or earthen pot with 200 ml of clean potable water, bring to a boil, and simmer gently over low heat for 10-15 minutes until the liquid reduces to about one-fourth to one-half of its original volume (approx. 50-75 ml).
Remove from heat, strain the decoction through a clean cotton cloth or fine mesh strainer into a cup, and allow it to cool to a comfortable lukewarm temperature.
Take 50 ml (approx. 3 tablespoons) of the warm strained decoction orally (twice daily for 3-5 days) for rheumatism.
storage: Consume fresh while warm; if needed, keep covered in a cool place and use within 12 hours.

traditionalUsage.typicalAdultAmount: 50 ml (approx. 3 tablespoons) of the warm strained decoction
traditionalUsage.typicalFrequency: twice daily for 3-5 days

doshaEffect: Pacifies aggravated Vata and Kapha in the musculoskeletal channels (Asthi-Majjavaha Srotas)

redFlagSymptoms: a hot, swollen joint with fever
sudden severe pain or inability to bear weight after injury
numbness, tingling or weakness in the limb
pain lasting more than a few weeks
stopAndSeeDoctorIf: These remedies are for adults. Do not give them to infants; for children, ask a clinician first.
If you are pregnant, breastfeeding, taking regular medicines, or have a long-term illness, ask a clinician before using this.

titleEn: Veeli (Cissampelos pareira) plant oil with rice flour for body pain
communityOrTradition: Malasar tribes, Coimbatore district
traditionalUses: traditionally applied for body pain relief

ingredients.name: Padh (whole plant)
ingredients.notes: Clean plant material for infusing into base oil

ingredients.name: Rice flour
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 teaspoon co-ingredient

ingredients.name: Sesame or coconut base oil
ingredients.notes: Traditional carrier oil for herbal infusion

steps: Weigh 15 g of clean whole plant of Padh (Cissampelos pareira), wash if fresh, and crush or grind into a coarse paste/powder.

Combine the 15 g of prepared whole plant and 5 g of Rice flour with 50 ml of sesame or coconut base oil in a heavy-bottomed pan and simmer gently over very low heat for 10-15 minutes until watery moisture evaporates and the active herbal principles infuse into the oil.
Remove from heat, allow the oil to cool completely, strain through a clean cotton cloth into a dry glass bottle, and test a drop on intact skin first.
Massage or apply 5-10 ml of the prepared medicated oil onto the affected area (once or twice daily for 5-7 days) for body pain relief.
storage: Store strained medicated oil in a clean, dry, tightly stoppered glass bottle away from sunlight for up to 3 months.

titleEn: Saathi saaranai (Trianthema decandra) root bark powder for muscle strength
communityOrTradition: Malasar tribes, Coimbatore district

ingredients.name: Saathi saaranai (root bark)
ingredients.notes: Approx. 0.5-1 level teaspoon of shade-dried, finely sieved powder (churna)

ingredients.name: Lukewarm potable water
ingredients.notes: 1 teacup of water for steeping/mixing

steps: Collect clean, mature root bark of Saathi saaranai (Trianthema decandra), dry thoroughly in the shade until completely moisture-free, and grind in a dry mortar or mill; sieve through a fine mesh to measure out 3 g of fine powder (churna).
Measure 150 ml of lukewarm potable water into a clean glass.
Stir the 3 g of fine herbal powder into the 150 ml of lukewarm water until evenly dispersed.
Take 3 g (approx. 0.5-1 level teaspoon) of herbal powder in vehicle orally (once or twice daily for 3-7 days) to strengthen muscles.
storage: Store the dry sieved powder in a clean, airtight glass jar away from moisture and sunlight for up to 2 months.

titleEn: Thuthi (Abutilon indicum) leaf juice for dental problems
communityOrTradition: Malayali tribes, Kolli hills, Namakkal district

ingredients.name: Thuthi (leaf)
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 handful of fresh, washed plant material (yields ~10 ml expressed juice)

ingredients.name: Clean boiled and cooled water
ingredients.notes: 1 tablespoon of water to aid mortar maceration/grinding

steps: Harvest or select 15 g (approx. 1 handful) of fresh, healthy leaf of Thuthi (Abutilon indicum), wash thoroughly under clean running water to remove dust, and drain excess moisture.
Transfer the 15 g of washed leaf to a clean stone mortar and pestle, add 15 ml of boiled and cooled water to moisten the tissue, and pound thoroughly into a wet macerated pulp.
Place the crushed pulp in a clean, folded muslin cloth and wring firmly into a small cup to collect approximately 10-15 ml (2-3 teaspoons) of fresh expressed juice/extract (swarasa).
Take 10 ml (2 teaspoons) of the freshly extracted liquid orally (Twice daily) for dental problems.
storage: Must be prepared fresh immediately before consumption; do not store expressed plant juice.

traditionalUsage.typicalAdultAmount: 10 ml (2 teaspoons) of the freshly extracted liquid
traditionalUsage.typicalFrequency: Twice daily
traditionalUsage.traditionalTiming: Morning on an empty stomach or after light food

doshaEffect: Balances Kapha and Pitta in the oral cavity and throat (Kanthya and Mukharoga-hara)

drooling or inability to open the mouth
high fever with throat pain
mouth ulcers lasting more than 2 weeks

titleEn: Gaju chettu (Allophylus cobbe) root decoction for diarrhoea
communityOrTradition: Koya and Konda Reddi tribes, Khammam district, Telangana
traditionalUses: traditionally used for diarrhoea and dysentery

ingredients.name: Gaju chettu (root)
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 tablespoon / small handful of clean, coarsely crushed plant material

ingredients.name: Clean potable water
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 cup of water for boiling decoction

steps: Weigh 15 g of clean root of Gaju chettu (Allophylus cobbe), wash thoroughly under running potable water to remove any soil or surface debris, and chop or crush coarsely in a mortar.

Place the 15 g of crushed root into a clean stainless-steel or earthen pot with 200 ml of clean potable water, bring to a boil, and simmer gently over low heat for 10-15 minutes until the liquid reduces to about one-fourth to one-half of its original volume (approx. 50-75 ml).
Remove from heat, strain the decoction through a clean cotton cloth or fine mesh strainer into a cup, and allow it to cool to a comfortable lukewarm temperature.
Take 12 ml of root decoction orally (12 ml, three times daily for two days) for diarrhoea and dysentery.
storage: Consume fresh while warm; if needed, keep covered in a cool place and use within 12 hours.

titleEn: Pindi kura (Aerva lanata) leaves for wounds
communityOrTradition: Koya communities, Eturnagaram Wildlife Sanctuary, Warangal district, Telangana

ingredients.name: Gedua ki chal (leaf)
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 tablespoon of fresh, washed plant material for grinding into paste

ingredients.name: Clean boiled and cooled water
ingredients.notes: 1 tablespoon of water to aid mortar maceration/grinding

steps: Select 15 g of clean leaf of Gedua ki chal (Aerva lanata) and wash thoroughly under running potable water to remove all surface dirt.
Crush and grind the 15 g of leaf in a clean stone mortar with 15 ml of clean water until a smooth, thick paste is formed.
Clean the affected skin area gently with potable water, pat dry with a clean cloth, and test a small dab of the preparation on intact skin first to check for sensitivity.

Apply 10-15 g of the prepared paste (sufficient to coat the affected area) externally over the affected site (once or twice daily for 3-5 days) for wounds, and rinse off gently with lukewarm water after 30-45 minutes.
storage: Grind fresh paste for each application; discard any unused wet paste after use.

titleEn: Konda patti (Kydia calycina) bark for dyspepsia
communityOrTradition: Koya communities, Eturnagaram Wildlife Sanctuary, Warangal district, Telangana

ingredients.name: Konda patti (bark)
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 tablespoon / small handful of clean, coarsely crushed plant material

ingredients.name: Clean potable water
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 cup of water for boiling decoction

steps: Weigh 15 g of clean bark of Konda patti (Kydia calycina), wash thoroughly under running potable water to remove any soil or surface debris, and chop or crush coarsely in a mortar.

Place the 15 g of crushed bark into a clean stainless-steel or earthen pot with 200 ml of clean potable water, bring to a boil, and simmer gently over low heat for 10-15 minutes until the liquid reduces to about one-fourth to one-half of its original volume (approx. 50-75 ml).
Remove from heat, strain the decoction through a clean cotton cloth or fine mesh strainer into a cup, and allow it to cool to a comfortable lukewarm temperature.
Take 50 ml (approx. 3 tablespoons) of the warm strained decoction orally (twice daily for 3-5 days) for dyspepsia.
storage: Consume fresh while warm; if needed, keep covered in a cool place and use within 12 hours.

steps: Select 15 g of clean leaf of Yadaku (Combretum decandrum) and wash thoroughly under running potable water to remove all surface dirt.

titleEn: Mullathotakura (Amaranthus spinosus) plant decoction for dysentery

steps: Weigh 15 g of clean whole plant of Kantewali Chaulai (Amaranthus spinosus), wash thoroughly under running potable water to remove any soil or surface debris, and chop or crush coarsely in a mortar.

Remove from heat, strain the decoction through a clean cotton cloth or fine mesh strainer into a cup, and allow it to cool to a comfortable lukewarm temperature.
Take 50 ml (approx. 3 tablespoons) of the warm strained decoction orally (twice daily for 3-5 days) for dysentery.
storage: Consume fresh while warm; if needed, keep covered in a cool place and use within 12 hours.

titleEn: Titepate (Artemisia indica) leaf and twig extract for throat pain, cold and cough
communityOrTradition: Gorkha Nepalese communities of Darjeeling Hills, West Bengal
traditionalUses: traditionally used for throat pain, cold and cough

ingredients.name: Titepate (fresh leaf and twig)
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 tablespoon / small handful of clean, coarsely crushed plant material

ingredients.name: Clean potable water
ingredients.notes: Approx. 1 cup of water for boiling decoction

steps: Weigh 15 g of clean fresh leaf and twig of Titepate (Artemisia indica), wash thoroughly under running potable water to remove any soil or surface debris, and chop or crush coarsely in a mortar.

Place the 15 g of crushed fresh leaf and twig into a clean stainless-steel or earthen pot with 200 ml of clean potable water, bring to a boil, and simmer gently over low heat for 10-15 minutes until the liquid reduces to about one-fourth to one-half of its original volume (approx. 50-75 ml).
Remove from heat, strain the decoction through a clean cotton cloth or fine mesh strainer into a cup, and allow it to cool to a comfortable lukewarm temperature.
Take 1 teaspoon of fresh leaf-and-twig extract orally (for 3 to 7 days, preferably in the morning after food) for throat pain, cold and cough.
storage: Consume fresh while warm; if needed, keep covered in a cool place and use within 12 hours.

steps: Using kitchen tongs or gloves to avoid stinging hairs, select 100 g of tender Sishnu (Urtica dioica) leaves, twigs, and inflorescence and wash thoroughly under running water.

Transfer the 100 g of cleaned nettle greens into a pot with 300 ml of boiling water and cook over medium heat for 5-10 minutes until the stinging hairs are completely neutralized and the greens are soft.
Mash or stir the cooked greens into a thick broth and mix in 5 g (1 teaspoon) of cow ghee and 1 g of rock salt.
Take 150-200 ml (1 bowl) of the warm nettle soup orally with meals (once daily for 3-5 days) for gastric discomfort.

titleEn: Shatavari Root Milk Decoction (Ksheerapaka) for Postpartum Lactation
communityOrTradition: All-India Classical & Household Tradition — Traditional Pan-Indian Ayurvedic Stanyajanana milk decoction using Asparagus racemosus root
traditionalUses: Traditionally used for postpartum hypogalactia (low breast milk supply) and maternal weakness

Warm medicated milk decoction (Ksheerapaka) of Shatavari (Asparagus racemosus) root powder gently simmered in cow's milk and water with raw cane sugar to support postpartum lactation (Stanyajanana) and maternal recovery.

ingredients.name: Dried Shatavari tuberous root powder (Asparagus racemosus)
ingredients.notes: 5 g (approx. 1 level teaspoon) — Finely sieved root churna

ingredients.name: Whole cow's milk (Godugdha)
ingredients.notes: 150 ml (approx. 1 teacup) — Fresh whole milk

ingredients.name: Drinking water
ingredients.notes: 150 ml (approx. 1 teacup) — For Ksheerapaka reduction

ingredients.name: Unrefined cane sugar or rock sugar (Mishri)
ingredients.notes: 5 g (approx. 1 teaspoon) — Added after simmering

steps: Measure 5 g of dried Shatavari root powder into a heavy-bottomed stainless steel saucepan. (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: Break up any clumps before adding liquids.)

Pour in 150 ml of whole cow's milk and 150 ml of drinking water, stirring thoroughly to disperse the root powder. (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: Equal parts milk and water allow slow extraction without scorching.)

Simmer gently over low heat for 12 to 15 minutes while stirring occasionally until the water evaporates and the volume reduces back to 150 ml of infused milk. (Duration: ~13 min. Tip: Keep the flame low so the milk does not boil over.)
Strain through a fine mesh strainer into a cup, stir in 5 g of rock sugar while warm, and drink. (Duration: ~3 min. Tip: Consume lukewarm around 40°C.)
storage: Consume warm immediately; refrigerate up to 6 hours if needed. (Maximum shelf life: 6 hours).

traditionalUsage.typicalAdultAmount: 150 ml of warm medicated milk containing 5 g of Shatavari root extract per serving.
traditionalUsage.typicalFrequency: Twice daily (morning and bedtime) for 30 to 45 days during the postpartum nursing period

doshaEffect: Pacifies Vata and Pitta doshas; nourishes Rasa and Stanya (breast milk) dhatus

high postpartum fever (above 38 C), chills, or foul-smelling lochia

Simmer over low heat for 15 minutes until the liquid reduces to one-fourth volume (approximately 50 ml). (Duration: ~15 min. Tip: Stir twice during boiling.)
Filter through a clean cotton cloth, allow the decoction to cool to lukewarm (below 40°C), and stir in 5 ml of honey before serving. (Duration: ~5 min. Tip: Never add honey to boiling hot liquid.)

Simmer on low flame for 7 to 8 minutes until the water turns golden-amber and reduces to about 400 ml. (Duration: ~8 min. Tip: Simmering covered preserves the carminative oils.)
Strain into an insulated flask and sip 150 ml to 200 ml warm after meals. (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: Drink warm rather than cold during the 40-day postpartum window.)
storage: Store in a thermos flask to sip warm throughout the day up to 12 hours. (Maximum shelf life: 12 hours).

titleEn: Mangrail / Kalonji (Nigella sativa) & Jaggery Decoction for Postpartum Uterine Cleansing
communityOrTradition: Santhal, Tharu, Oraon — Traditional Bihar and Jharkhand tribal maternal tonic for lochia expulsion and lactation
traditionalUses: Traditionally used for postpartum sluggish uterine involution, retained lochia, and hypogalactia

Warm spiced decoction of black cumin / Mangrail seeds (Nigella sativa) simmered with ginger and jaggery, given to new mothers in Bihar and Eastern India to stimulate uterine contraction after birth and enhance breast milk production.

ingredients.name: Kalonji / Mangrail seeds (Nigella sativa)
ingredients.notes: 3 g (approx. 1/2 level teaspoon, crushed) — Lightly toasted and crushed

ingredients.name: Fresh ginger rhizome (Zingiber officinale)
ingredients.notes: 2 g (grated) — Synergistic warming herb

ingredients.name: Drinking water
ingredients.notes: 200 ml (approx. 1 glass) — Reduced to 100 ml

ingredients.name: Unrefined jaggery (Gud)
ingredients.notes: 10 g (approx. 2 teaspoons) — Added at the end of boiling

steps: Lightly dry-roast 3 g of Nigella sativa seeds for 30 seconds and crush coarsely in a mortar. (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: Do not over-roast as the seeds are already dark.)
Combine the crushed Kalonji seeds and 2 g of grated ginger with 200 ml of water in a small pot. (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: Cover partially with a lid.)
Simmer over low heat for 10 to 12 minutes until the liquid reduces by half to 100 ml. (Duration: ~11 min. Tip: Gentle simmering extracts thymoquinone.)
Stir in 10 g of jaggery until dissolved, strain through a fine sieve, and drink warm. (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: Take once daily in the morning.)
storage: Consume warm; keep covered up to 8 hours. (Maximum shelf life: 8 hours).

traditionalUsage.typicalAdultAmount: 100 ml of warm strained decoction once daily.
traditionalUsage.typicalFrequency: Once daily for 7 to 14 days postpartum

doshaEffect: Pacifies Kapha and Vata; Garbhashaya Vishodhana (uterine purifier) and Stanyajanana

high postpartum fever (above 38 C), chills, or foul-smelling lochia
severe lower abdominal or pelvic pain that does not ease
red, hot, wedge-shaped painful breast swelling (mastitis) or severe calf pain/shortness of breath
stopAndSeeDoctorIf: Seek immediate obstetric or medical care if you experience heavy bleeding, high fever, severe pelvic pain, or signs of postpartum infection.

titleEn: Kumari (Aloe vera) Fresh Inner Gel with Black Pepper for Painful or Scanty Menses
communityOrTradition: Meena, Bhil, Lambadi — Traditional Rajasthani and Telangana ethnomedicinal emmenagogue preparation
traditionalUses: Traditionally used for dysmenorrhoea (painful menstruation) and oligomenorrhoea (scanty flow)

Freshly filleted, thoroughly washed inner translucent mucilaginous gel of Kumari (Aloe vera) seasoned with a pinch of crushed black pepper and turmeric to ease spasmodic menstrual cramps and promote healthy menstrual flow.

ingredients.name: Fresh washed inner translucent gel of Aloe vera
ingredients.notes: 15 g (approx. 1 tablespoon) — Yellow aloin latex completely washed off under running water

ingredients.name: Crushed black pepper (Piper nigrum)
ingredients.notes: 1 g (approx. 1/4 teaspoon) — Warming Anupana

ingredients.name: Turmeric powder (Curcuma longa)
ingredients.notes: 1 g (approx. 1/4 teaspoon) — Anti-spasmodic adjunct

ingredients.name: Unrefined jaggery or honey
ingredients.notes: 5 g (approx. 1 teaspoon) — Improves palatability

steps: Cut a mature Aloe vera leaf, stand it upright for 10 minutes to let the bitter yellow latex drain out completely, then peel away the green rind. (Duration: ~5 min. Tip: Removing the yellow rind sap prevents intestinal cramping.)
Scoop 15 g of the clear inner fillet and rinse it 3 times in clean drinking water. (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: The gel should be completely clear and non-bitter.)
Mash the 15 g of washed gel in a small bowl with 1 g of black pepper, 1 g of turmeric powder, and 5 g of jaggery. (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: Mix into a uniform spoonful.)
Consume immediately in the morning followed by a few sips of lukewarm water. (Duration: ~1 min. Tip: Take for 3 to 5 days prior to or during painful menses.)
storage: Prepare immediately before consumption; do not store washed raw gel for more than 2 hours. (Maximum shelf life: 2 hours).

traditionalUsage.typicalAdultAmount: 15 g of washed inner Aloe gel mixture once daily.

titleEn: Babool Gond (Vachellia nilotica) Edible Gum in Warm Milk for Postpartum Backache
communityOrTradition: Haryanvi Rural & Ahir Tradition — Traditional Haryanvi and North Indian maternal bone and pelvic strengthening tonic
traditionalUses: Traditionally used for postpartum lower back pain, pelvic joint laxity, and physical exhaustion

Nourishing warm drink prepared by puffing edible acacia gum (Gond of Vachellia nilotica) in cow's ghee, crushing the crisp crystals, and simmering them in warm milk with jaggery to strengthen the spine and pelvic floor after childbirth.

ingredients.name: Edible Babool gum crystals / Gond (Vachellia nilotica)
ingredients.notes: 5 g (approx. 1 teaspoon small crystals) — Clean amber food-grade Gond

ingredients.name: Pure cow's ghee (Clarified butter)
ingredients.notes: 5 ml (approx. 1 teaspoon) — For puffing the gum

ingredients.name: Whole cow's milk
ingredients.notes: 150 ml (approx. 1 teacup) — Warm milk

ingredients.name: Unrefined jaggery or raw cane sugar (Bura)
ingredients.notes: 10 g (approx. 2 teaspoons) — Added at the end

steps: Heat 5 ml of cow's ghee in a small pan over medium-low heat and add 5 g of small Babool Gond crystals, stirring for 1 to 2 minutes until they puff up and turn opaque and crisp. (Duration: ~3 min. Tip: Keep the heat moderate so the inside of each crystal puffs completely.)
Transfer the puffed Gond onto a plate and crush coarsely with the back of a spoon. (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: Properly puffed Gond crushes effortlessly.)
Pour 150 ml of cow's milk into the pan, add the crushed puffed Gond, and simmer gently for 5 minutes until creamy. (Duration: ~5 min. Tip: Stir continuously.)
Remove from heat, stir in 10 g of raw cane sugar or jaggery, and drink warm. (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: Best taken in the morning or evening during postpartum confinement.)
storage: Consume warm immediately after preparation. (Maximum shelf life: 6 hours).

traditionalUsage.typicalAdultAmount: 150 ml of warm Gond milk containing 5 g of puffed edible gum.
traditionalUsage.typicalFrequency: Once daily for 21 to 40 days postpartum

titleEn: Jamyrdoh (Houttuynia cordata) Tender Shoot Broth for Postpartum Recovery
communityOrTradition: Khasi, Jaintia, Garo — Traditional Khasi and Jaintia matrilineal postpartum restorative from Meghalaya
traditionalUses: Traditionally used for postpartum fatigue, pelvic inflammation, and recovery after childbirth

Light, aromatic herbal broth prepared by simmering fresh tender shoots and leaves of Jamyrdoh (Houttuynia cordata) with ginger and black sesame to restore maternal vitality and soothe postpartum inflammation.

ingredients.name: Fresh tender leaves and shoots of Houttuynia cordata
ingredients.notes: 20 g (approx. 1 handful, chopped) — Rinsed thoroughly

ingredients.name: Fresh ginger rhizome (Zingiber officinale)
ingredients.notes: 3 g (sliced) — Warming digestive aid

ingredients.name: Toasted black sesame seeds (Sesamum indicum)
ingredients.notes: 5 g (approx. 1 teaspoon, crushed) — Traditional Khasi seasoning

ingredients.name: Drinking water
ingredients.notes: 200 ml (approx. 1 glass) — Simmered to 150 ml

steps: Wash 20 g of fresh Houttuynia cordata shoots and leaves in clean water and chop into 2 cm pieces. (Duration: ~4 min. Tip: Select young heart-shaped leaves.)
Bring 200 ml of water with 3 g of sliced ginger to a boil in a small pot. (Duration: ~3 min. Tip: Simmer ginger first for 2 minutes.)

Add the chopped Houttuynia cordata and 5 g of crushed toasted black sesame seeds, simmering gently for 6 to 7 minutes until reduced to 150 ml. (Duration: ~7 min. Tip: Brief simmering preserves volatile flavonoids.)
Serve warm as a clear herbal soup along with the tender greens. (Duration: ~1 min. Tip: Consume with midday or evening rice meal.)
storage: Consume warm immediately after cooking. (Maximum shelf life: 6 hours).

titleEn: Kala Rasi (Sesamum indicum) Black Sesame & Jaggery Paste for Delayed or Painful Menses
communityOrTradition: Kandha, Saora, Santal — Traditional Odisha tribal emmenagogue paste for Vata-type dysmenorrhoea and oligomenorrhoea
traditionalUses: Traditionally used for delayed, scanty, or painful menstruation (kashtartava / artavakshaya)

Warming stone-ground paste (Kalka) of lightly roasted black sesame seeds (Sesamum indicum) pounded with old unrefined jaggery and dry ginger, taken with warm water to relieve spasmodic menstrual cramps and initiate delayed flow.

ingredients.name: Unpolished black sesame seeds (Sesamum indicum)
ingredients.notes: 10 g (approx. 2 teaspoons) — Cleaned and lightly toasted

ingredients.name: Unrefined old jaggery (Purana Guda)
ingredients.notes: 10 g (approx. 2 teaspoons) — Grated

ingredients.name: Dry ginger powder (Zingiber officinale)
ingredients.notes: 1 g (approx. 1/4 teaspoon) — Warming catalyst

ingredients.name: Warm drinking water
ingredients.notes: 150 ml (approx. 1 teacup) — Taken alongside the paste

steps: Dry-roast 10 g of black sesame seeds in a skillet over low heat for 1 to 2 minutes until they crackle lightly. (Duration: ~3 min. Tip: Use black sesame (Krishna Tila) rather than white sesame for menstrual care.)
Pound the warm sesame seeds with 1 g of dry ginger powder in a stone mortar into a coarse powder. (Duration: ~3 min. Tip: Avoid over-grinding into liquid oil before adding jaggery.)
Add 10 g of grated jaggery and pound together for 2 minutes until a cohesive paste ball forms. (Duration: ~3 min. Tip: The natural oil of sesame binds seamlessly with jaggery.)
Chew the 21 g paste ball thoroughly and follow with 150 ml of warm water. (Duration: ~3 min. Tip: Take in the morning starting 3 days before expected menses.)
storage: Store in a dry glass jar up to 48 hours; consume with warm water. (Maximum shelf life: 48 hours).

traditionalUsage.typicalFrequency: Once daily in the morning for 3 to 5 days prior to and during onset of menstruation

titleEn: Nirgundi (Vitex negundo) Warm Leaf Bath Decoction for Postpartum Body Ache & Perineal Care
communityOrTradition: Bhil, Pawara, Kokni — Traditional Maharashtrian & Bhil Sutika Snana (postpartum herbal bath) for Vata pacification
traditionalUses: Traditionally used for postpartum generalized body ache, joint stiffness, and perineal soreness

Aromatic external herbal bath decoction prepared by boiling fresh leaves of Nirgundi (Vitex negundo) with neem leaves and rock salt in water, used for warm sponge bathing and pelvic fomentation (Avagaha/Parisheka) during postpartum recovery.

ingredients.name: Fresh Vitex negundo (Nirgundi) leaves
ingredients.notes: 100 g (approx. 2 large handfuls) — Rinsed and lightly bruised

ingredients.name: Fresh Azadirachta indica (Neem) leaves
ingredients.notes: 25 g (approx. 1 small handful) — Antiseptic botanical adjunct

ingredients.name: Rock salt (Saindhava Lavana)
ingredients.notes: 10 g (approx. 2 teaspoons) — Soothes muscle soreness

ingredients.name: Water for boiling
ingredients.notes: 2000 ml (2 liters) — Diluted with warm bath water before use

steps: Rinse 100 g of fresh Vitex negundo leaves and 25 g of neem leaves thoroughly and crush them lightly by hand. (Duration: ~5 min. Tip: Bruising the leaves releases aromatic cineole and caryophyllene oils.)
Place the leaves in a large pot with 2000 ml of water and bring to a rolling boil. (Duration: ~5 min. Tip: Keep the pot covered so steam does not escape.)
Simmer covered for 15 minutes until the water turns dark olive-green and fragrant, then stir in 10 g of rock salt. (Duration: ~15 min. Tip: The aroma should be strongly camphoraceous and herbal.)

Strain the hot decoction into a bath bucket or sitz basin, allow to cool to a comfortable warm temperature (40°C), and use for external warm sponge bathing or lower-back fomentation. (Duration: ~5 min. Tip: For external use only; pat skin dry and keep warm afterward.)
storage: Use warm immediately for external bathing/fomentation; do not store past 6 hours. (Maximum shelf life: 6 hours).
