titleEn: Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera) Warm Root Milk (Ksheerapaka) for Insomnia & Stress
communityOrTradition: All-India Classical & Household Tradition — Classical Pan-Indian Ayurvedic Nidrajanana (sleep-inducing) bedtime milk decoction
traditionalUses: Traditionally used for anidra (insomnia), stress-induced restlessness, and mental exhaustion

Soothing bedtime milk decoction (Ksheerapaka) prepared by simmering Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera) root powder with a pinch of green cardamom in cow's milk and water to lower evening cortisol, calm aggravated Vata, and promote deep restorative sleep.

ingredients.name: Fine Ashwagandha root powder (Withania somnifera)
ingredients.notes: 4 g (approx. 1 level teaspoon) — Nagori Ashwagandha root churna

ingredients.name: Crushed green cardamom pods (Elettaria cardamomum)
ingredients.notes: 1 g (approx. 2 pods) — Aromatic digestive aid

ingredients.name: Whole cow's milk
ingredients.notes: 150 ml (approx. 1 teacup) — Warm whole milk

ingredients.name: Drinking water
ingredients.notes: 100 ml (approx. 2/3 cup) — Evaporated during simmering

ingredients.name: Rock sugar (Mishri)
ingredients.notes: 5 g (approx. 1 teaspoon) — Added after straining

steps: Whisk 4 g of Ashwagandha root powder and 1 g of crushed cardamom into 150 ml of cow's milk and 100 ml of water in a small saucepan. (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: Mixing before heating prevents root powder lumps.)
Bring to a gentle simmer over low heat. (Duration: ~3 min. Tip: Keep the flame low.)
Simmer gently for 9 to 10 minutes until the added water evaporates and 150 ml of fragrant milk remains. (Duration: ~9 min. Tip: Stir occasionally to prevent skin formation.)
Strain into a mug, dissolve 5 g of rock sugar, and sip warm 30 minutes before sleep. (Duration: ~3 min. Tip: Avoid screen exposure after drinking.)
storage: Drink warm 30 minutes before bedtime; do not store past 4 hours. (Maximum shelf life: 4 hours).

traditionalUsage.typicalAdultAmount: 150 ml of warm medicated milk containing 4 g of Ashwagandha root.
traditionalUsage.typicalFrequency: Once daily at bedtime for 30 to 60 days
traditionalUsage.traditionalTiming: 30 minutes before bedtime (at least 1.5 hours after dinner)

doshaEffect: Pacifies Vata and Kapha; Rasayana, Balya, and Nidrajanana (promotes deep sleep)

loud snoring with pauses in breathing or gasping at night (sleep apnea)

stopAndSeeDoctorIf: Consult a qualified physician if sleeplessness persists beyond 3 weeks or is accompanied by severe anxiety, depression, or breathing pauses during sleep.

titleEn: Jatamansi (Nardostachys jatamansi) Rhizome Warm Infusion (Phanta) for Deep Sleep
communityOrTradition: Bhotiya, Jaunsari, Garhwali — Traditional Uttarakhand Himalayan Bhotiya & classical Ayurvedic Medhya calming infusion
traditionalUses: Traditionally used for chronic insomnia (anidra), racing thoughts, and nervous agitation

Aromatic warm infusion (Phanta) steeped from the coarse rhizome of Himalayan spikenard (Nardostachys jatamansi), revered in Uttarakhand and classical Ayurveda to quiet racing thoughts (Chittodvega) and induce natural sleep.

ingredients.name: Coarsely crushed rhizome of Nardostachys jatamansi
ingredients.notes: 3 g (approx. 1/2 to 3/4 level teaspoon) — Cultivated/sustainably sourced rhizome powder

ingredients.name: Hot boiled water
ingredients.notes: 150 ml (approx. 1 teacup) — Just off the boil (approx. 90°C)

ingredients.name: Pure wild honey (Madhu)
ingredients.notes: 5 ml (approx. 1 teaspoon) — Added after cooling to lukewarm

steps: Place 3 g of coarsely crushed Nardostachys jatamansi rhizome into a ceramic or glass cup. (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: Never boil Jatamansi over an open flame, as its calming jatamansone sesquiterpenes are heat-volatile.)
Pour 150 ml of freshly boiled water over the herb and immediately cover the cup with a tight lid or saucer. (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: Covering traps the woody, musky essential oil.)
Allow to steep covered for 10 minutes until the infusion cools to lukewarm. (Duration: ~10 min. Tip: Swirl the cup gently before straining.)
Strain through a fine cloth, stir in 5 ml of honey, and drink slowly 30 minutes before bedtime. (Duration: ~1 min. Tip: Inhale the calming aroma while sipping.)
storage: Steep covered and drink warm before sleep; do not boil vigorously. (Maximum shelf life: 6 hours).

Warm evening infusion of Indian Valerian (Valeriana jatamansi / Tagara) root powder steeped with fennel seeds to relax skeletal muscle tension, pacify Vata-type anxiety, and shorten sleep onset time.

ingredients.notes: 2 g (approx. 1/2 level teaspoon) — Shade-dried root powder

Steep covered for 8 to 10 minutes. (Duration: ~9 min. Tip: Stir once before straining.)
Strain through a fine mesh, add 3 g of Mishri if desired, and drink warm 30 minutes before going to bed. (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: Avoid operating machinery after consumption.)

titleEn: Shankhapushpi (Convolvulus prostratus) Medhya Milk Drink for Anxiety & Restful Sleep

traditionalUses: Traditionally used for mental restlessness, exam/work anxiety, and light fragmented sleep

Cooling, calming evening drink prepared by mixing whole-plant powder of desert Shankhapushpi (Convolvulus prostratus) into warm cow's milk with rock sugar to soothe mental agitation and deepen sleep quality.

ingredients.name: Fine whole-plant powder of Convolvulus prostratus (Shankhapushpi)
ingredients.notes: 3 g (approx. 1/2 to 3/4 level teaspoon) — Shade-dried flowering whole herb powder

ingredients.name: Warm cow's milk
ingredients.notes: 150 ml (approx. 1 teacup) — Heated to 60°C

ingredients.name: Rock sugar (Mishri)
ingredients.notes: 5 g (approx. 1 teaspoon) — Cooling sweetener

steps: Heat 150 ml of cow's milk in a small saucepan until hot and steaming (about 3 minutes), then remove from the flame. (Duration: ~3 min. Tip: Do not boil Shankhapushpi powder for a long time.)
Measure 3 g of fine Shankhapushpi whole-plant powder and 5 g of rock sugar into a cup. (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: Sieve the churna if coarse.)
Pour 30 ml of the warm milk into the cup first and whisk into a smooth paste, then pour in the remaining 120 ml of warm milk. (Duration: ~3 min. Tip: Let steep for 3 minutes.)
Drink lukewarm 30 to 45 minutes before bedtime. (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: May be strained through a tea strainer if preferred.)
storage: Prepare fresh before bedtime and consume immediately. (Maximum shelf life: 4 hours).

communityOrTradition: Kani, Classical Kerala Ayurveda Tradition — Traditional Kerala Ayurvedic nervine tonic for mental fatigue and stress-induced insomnia
traditionalUses: Traditionally used for stress-induced insomnia, nervous exhaustion, and restlessness

Calming evening preparation combining freshly expressed juice (Swarasa) or steeped leaves of wetland Brahmi (Bacopa monnieri) with warm cow's milk and a drop of ghee to soothe Sadhaka Pitta and Prana Vata.

ingredients.name: Fresh succulent leaves and stems of Bacopa monnieri
ingredients.notes: 10 g (approx. 1 small handful, yields 5 ml juice) — Thoroughly washed in drinking water

ingredients.name: Warm cow's milk
ingredients.notes: 150 ml (approx. 1 teacup) — Buffers the natural bitterness of Brahmi

ingredients.name: Pure cow's ghee
ingredients.notes: 3 ml (approx. 1/2 teaspoon) — Lipid carrier for bacosides

ingredients.name: Rock sugar (Mishri)
ingredients.notes: 5 g (approx. 1 teaspoon) — Sweetener

steps: Wash 10 g of fresh Bacopa monnieri stems and leaves thoroughly in clean drinking water. (Duration: ~4 min. Tip: Since Brahmi grows in marshy areas, rinse 3 times in boiled-and-cooled water.)

Pound the fresh leaves in a stone mortar and squeeze through a clean muslin cloth to extract 5 ml of fresh green juice (or simmer the crushed leaves directly in the milk for 5 minutes). (Duration: ~5 min. Tip: Simmering in milk is recommended if fresh leaves are from outdoor beds.)

Stir the Brahmi extract, 3 ml of cow's ghee, and 5 g of rock sugar into 150 ml of warm cow's milk. (Duration: ~3 min. Tip: Ghee enhances the blood-brain barrier absorption of lipid-soluble bacosides.)
Drink lukewarm in the evening after dinner. (Duration: ~3 min. Tip: Take consistently for 2 to 4 weeks.)
storage: Consume immediately after extracting fresh leaf juice and mixing with warm milk. (Maximum shelf life: 4 hours).

titleEn: Jaiphal (Myristica fragrans) Grated Nutmeg in Warm Bedtime Milk for Insomnia
communityOrTradition: Konkani, Maratha, Warli — Time-tested Maharashtrian & Konkan household bedtime nightcap for deep sleep
traditionalUses: Traditionally used for difficulty falling asleep and frequent nighttime awakenings

Fragrant, soothing bedtime milk prepared by simmering a measured micro-pinch (0.5 g) of freshly grated nutmeg kernel (Myristica fragrans / Jatiphala) with cow's milk and ghee to gently induce deep, uninterrupted sleep.

ingredients.name: Freshly grated nutmeg kernel / Jaiphal (Myristica fragrans)
ingredients.notes: 0.5 g (approx. 1/8 level teaspoon / 1 small pinch) — Grate fresh from a whole nutmeg kernel; never exceed 0.5 g

ingredients.name: Whole cow's milk
ingredients.notes: 150 ml (approx. 1 teacup) — Fresh whole milk

ingredients.name: Pure cow's ghee
ingredients.notes: 2 ml (approx. 1/2 teaspoon) — Prevents dryness associated with Vata

ingredients.name: Unrefined sugar or jaggery
ingredients.notes: 5 g (approx. 1 teaspoon) — To taste

steps: Rub a whole dried nutmeg kernel against a fine grater or grinding stone (Sahan) to collect exactly 0.5 g (1/8 teaspoon) of fresh nutmeg powder. (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: Freshly grated nutmeg retains myristicin and elemicin volatile oils lost in pre-ground spice jars.)
Pour 150 ml of cow's milk into a small saucepan and bring to a gentle boil. (Duration: ~3 min. Tip: Use low-medium heat.)
Add the 0.5 g of grated nutmeg and 2 ml of cow's ghee, simmering on low flame for 2 minutes. (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: Brief simmering infuses the warm aroma into the milk fat.)
Pour into a cup, stir in 5 g of sugar, and drink warm 30 minutes before lying down to sleep. (Duration: ~1 min. Tip: Keep the bedroom dim and quiet afterward.)
storage: Consume warm immediately 30 minutes before sleep. (Maximum shelf life: 2 hours).

ingredients.notes: 2 g (approx. 6 to 8 berries, lightly bruised) — Rich in calming citral essential oil

Place the bruised berries in a cup and pour 150 ml of hot boiled water over them. (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: Cover the cup immediately.)
Steep covered for 8 minutes until the water becomes fragrant and pale golden. (Duration: ~8 min. Tip: Do not boil over high heat.)
Strain out the berries, stir in 5 ml of honey once lukewarm, and sip 30 minutes before sleep. (Duration: ~1 min. Tip: Inhale the soothing citrus steam while drinking.)

ingredients.notes: 15 g (approx. 10 to 12 fresh leaves, shredded) — Washed thoroughly

Place the shredded leaves and 2 g of sliced ginger into a ceramic mug or teapot. (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: Warm the mug first with hot water.)
Pour 150 ml of freshly boiled water over the herbs, cover with a lid, and steep for 8 minutes. (Duration: ~8 min. Tip: Covering retains volatile methyl nonyl ketone and bornyl acetate.)
Strain and drink warm 45 minutes after dinner for relaxation and restful sleep. (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: May also be eaten lightly steamed with evening rice.)

ingredients.notes: 10 g (approx. 15 fresh fan-shaped leaves) — Washed thoroughly in clean water

ingredients.name: Crushed black pepper (Piper nigrum)
ingredients.notes: 0.5 g (approx. 2 peppercorns) — Prevents Kapha heaviness

Place the bruised leaves and pepper in a saucepan with 50 ml of water and 150 ml of cow's milk. (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: Stir well.)
Simmer over low flame for 8 to 10 minutes until the water evaporates and 150 ml of pale green-tinted milk remains. (Duration: ~9 min. Tip: Do not boil over high heat.)
Strain into a cup, dissolve 5 g of rock sugar, and drink warm 30 minutes before bedtime. (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: Ideal for students and elders experiencing restless sleep.)

titleEn: Bhringraj (Eclipta prostrata) Infused Sesame Oil Crown Massage (Shiroabhyanga) for Insomnia
communityOrTradition: Classical Kerala Ayurveda & Kalari Tradition — Classical Kerala Ayurvedic Murdhataila (crown & foot oiling) therapy for deep sleep
traditionalUses: Traditionally used for insomnia (anidra), tension headaches, and nocturnal eye strain

Traditional medicated oil prepared by simmering fresh juice and paste of Kayyonni / Bhringraj (Eclipta prostrata) in black sesame oil, massaged gently onto the crown of the head (Adhipati Marma) and soles of the feet before bedtime to induce sound sleep.

ingredients.name: Fresh Eclipta prostrata (Bhringraj) leaves and stems
ingredients.notes: 50 g (crushed for juice and paste) — Washed and drained

ingredients.name: Cold-pressed black sesame oil (Sesamum indicum)
ingredients.notes: 100 ml (approx. 1/2 cup) — Unrefined Gingelly oil

steps: Wash 50 g of fresh Eclipta prostrata herbs, pound in a stone mortar with 20 ml of water, and press to extract the dark green juice and fine herbal paste. (Duration: ~10 min. Tip: Bhringraj juice naturally oxidizes to a deep blackish-green color on contact with air.)
Combine 100 ml of cold-pressed sesame oil with the Bhringraj juice and paste in a heavy brass or steel pan. (Duration: ~3 min. Tip: Heat over the lowest flame setting.)

Simmer gently on low heat for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until all water moisture evaporates and the herbal sediment turns crisp without burning (Madhyama Paka). (Duration: ~22 min. Tip: Test a pinch of sediment: it should roll between fingers without crackling when exposed to flame.)

Cool completely, strain through a clean cotton cloth into a glass bottle, and massage 5 ml to 10 ml lukewarm onto the crown of the scalp (Bregma/Adhipati Marma) and soles of the feet 20 minutes before sleep. (Duration: ~5 min. Tip: External application only.)
storage: Store in an amber glass bottle in a cool, dry cupboard for up to 30 days (720 hours). (Maximum shelf life: 720 hours).

traditionalUsage.typicalAdultAmount: 5 ml to 10 ml of lukewarm medicated oil massaged onto the scalp crown and soles of the feet.
traditionalUsage.typicalFrequency: Once daily at bedtime for 14 to 30 days

communityOrTradition: Irula, Tamil Siddha & Household Tradition — Traditional Tamil Nadu & classical Ayurvedic Hima Kalpana for Pitta-type sleeplessness
traditionalUses: Traditionally used for pitta-type insomnia, night sweats, burning sensation, and summer restlessness

Fragrant cold-water root infusion (Hima) prepared by steeping cleaned roots of Vettiver / Ushira (Chrysopogon zizanioides) in drinking water stored in an earthen pot, sipped in the evening to cool internal Pitta heat and calm restlessness.

ingredients.name: Cleaned dried aromatic roots of Chrysopogon zizanioides (Vetiver)
ingredients.notes: 5 g (approx. 1 small tied bundle) — Rinsed free of soil

ingredients.name: Crushed coriander seeds (Coriandrum sativum)
ingredients.notes: 2 g (approx. 1/2 teaspoon) — Synergistic Pitta-cooling seed

ingredients.name: Room-temperature boiled-and-cooled drinking water
ingredients.notes: 300 ml (approx. 2 teacups) — Steeped in a clay or glass vessel

ingredients.name: Rock sugar (Karkandu / Mishri)
ingredients.notes: 5 g (approx. 1 teaspoon) — Optional

steps: Rinse 5 g of dried Chrysopogon zizanioides (Vettiver) roots thoroughly under running water to remove any clinging sand, and bruise lightly. (Duration: ~3 min. Tip: Tie the fibrous roots into a neat knot so they are easy to remove.)

Place the Vettiver root bundle and 2 g of lightly crushed coriander seeds into an earthen pot or glass jar with 300 ml of room-temperature drinking water. (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: Cold infusion (Hima Kalpana) preserves cooling volatile khusimol oils.)
Cover and allow to steep at room temperature for 3 to 4 hours until the water becomes delicately earthy and aromatic. (Duration: ~5 min. Tip: Do not refrigerate to ice-cold temperatures.)
Strain 150 ml into a glass, dissolve 2.5 g of rock sugar if desired, and drink in the late afternoon and evening. (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: The root bundle can be dried and reused once more.)
storage: Keep covered in a clean clay or glass pitcher for up to 12 hours. (Maximum shelf life: 12 hours).

titleEn: Khus-Khus (Papaver somniferum) Culinary White Poppy Seed & Almond Bedtime Milk
communityOrTradition: North Indian Household & Unani-Ayurveda Tradition — Traditional North Indian & Old Delhi household nutritive nightcap for deep sleep
traditionalUses: Traditionally used for sleeplessness from physical fatigue, vata dryness, and racing mind

Creamy, comforting bedtime drink prepared by soaking culinary white poppy seeds (Khus-Khus / Khasatila) and peeled almonds, grinding them into a smooth paste, and simmering in cow's milk with cardamom to nourish Majja Dhatu (nervous system) and induce restful sleep.

ingredients.name: Culinary white poppy seeds / Khus-Khus (Papaver somniferum)
ingredients.notes: 5 g (approx. 1 level teaspoon) — Food-grade washed white culinary seeds

ingredients.name: Soaked and peeled sweet almonds (Prunus dulcis)
ingredients.notes: 5 g (approx. 4 almonds) — Skins removed after soaking

ingredients.name: Whole cow's milk
ingredients.notes: 150 ml (approx. 1 teacup) — Fresh whole milk

ingredients.name: Crushed green cardamom (Elettaria cardamomum)
ingredients.notes: 0.5 g (1 pod) — Aids digestion of nuts and seeds

ingredients.name: Rock sugar (Mishri)
ingredients.notes: 5 g (approx. 1 teaspoon) — To taste

steps: Soak 5 g of culinary white poppy seeds (Khus-Khus) and 5 g (4 kernels) of almonds in 30 ml of warm water for 30 minutes, then peel the almond skins. (Duration: ~5 min. Tip: Soaking softens the tiny poppy seeds so they grind into a velvety milk.)

Grind the soaked Khus-Khus and peeled almonds on a grinding stone (Sil-Batta) or blender with 20 ml of milk into a smooth white paste. (Duration: ~5 min. Tip: Grind until no gritty seed hulls remain.)

Stir the paste and 0.5 g of crushed cardamom into 130 ml of cow's milk in a saucepan and simmer gently over low heat for 6 to 8 minutes. (Duration: ~8 min. Tip: Stir continuously so the nutty paste does not stick to the bottom.)
Sweeten with 5 g of rock sugar and drink warm 30 minutes before sleep. (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: Sip slowly in a relaxed setting.)
storage: Serve warm immediately at bedtime. (Maximum shelf life: 4 hours).

traditionalUsage.typicalAdultAmount: 150 ml of warm Khus-Khus and almond milk at bedtime.
traditionalUsage.typicalFrequency: Once daily at night for 7 to 21 days

titleEn: Makhana (Euryale ferox) & Lotus Seed (Nelumbo nucifera) Calming Bedtime Milk
communityOrTradition: Mithila Household & Tharu Tradition — Traditional Mithila (Bihar) soothing evening kheer for palpitations, restlessness, and sleep
traditionalUses: Traditionally used for nighttime restlessness, anxiety palpitations, and light fragmented sleep

Light, soothing bedtime milk prepared by dry-roasting fox nuts / Makhana (Euryale ferox) and lotus seeds (Nelumbo nucifera), crushing them coarsely, and simmering in cow's milk with cardamom to calm the heart (Hridya) and promote peaceful sleep.

ingredients.name: Puffed Makhana / Fox nuts (Euryale ferox)
ingredients.notes: 10 g (approx. 12 to 15 puffed seeds) — Dry-roasted and coarsely crushed

ingredients.name: Dried lotus seed kernels / Kamal Gatta (Nelumbo nucifera)
ingredients.notes: 3 g (approx. 1/2 teaspoon powder) — Finely powdered

ingredients.name: Whole cow's milk
ingredients.notes: 150 ml (approx. 1 teacup) — Fresh whole milk

ingredients.name: Green cardamom powder (Elettaria cardamomum)
ingredients.notes: 0.5 g (1 pinch) — Aromatic

ingredients.name: Rock sugar (Mishri)
ingredients.notes: 5 g (approx. 1 teaspoon) — Sweetener

steps: Dry-roast 10 g of puffed Makhana in a pan over low heat for 3 minutes until crisp, then crush them into coarse flakes. (Duration: ~4 min. Tip: Roasting makes Makhana light to digest at night.)
Bring 150 ml of cow's milk to a gentle boil in a saucepan and add the crushed Makhana and 3 g of lotus seed powder. (Duration: ~3 min. Tip: Stir to prevent clumping.)
Simmer on low flame for 6 to 7 minutes until the Makhana softens into the warm milk. (Duration: ~7 min. Tip: Add 0.5 g of cardamom powder in the final minute.)
Remove from heat, dissolve 5 g of rock sugar, and consume warm 45 minutes before bedtime. (Duration: ~1 min. Tip: Serves as a light, calming late-evening tonic.)
storage: Serve warm in the evening; store covered up to 6 hours. (Maximum shelf life: 6 hours).

titleEn: Jyotishmati / Malkangani (Celastrus paniculatus) Seed Oil Foot Massage (Padabhyanga) for Insomnia
communityOrTradition: Lepcha, Bhutia, Nepali — Traditional Sikkim Lepcha & classical Ayurvedic nervine oil rub for nocturnal Vata calming
traditionalUses: Traditionally used for chronic vata insomnia, cold feet at night, and nervous exhaustion

Warming topical foot massage oil prepared by diluting potent Malkangani / Jyotishmati seed oil (Celastrus paniculatus) in warm sesame oil, rubbed vigorously into the soles of the feet and Achilles tendons before bed to ground Prana Vata and induce deep sleep.

ingredients.name: Pure Celastrus paniculatus (Jyotishmati / Malkangani) seed oil
ingredients.notes: 1 ml (approx. 15 to 20 drops) — Potent ruby-brown seed oil

ingredients.name: Cold-pressed sesame oil (Sesamum indicum)
ingredients.notes: 9 ml (approx. 2 teaspoons) — Carrier oil for topical massage

steps: Wash both feet in warm water for 3 minutes and pat completely dry with a clean towel. (Duration: ~3 min. Tip: Warming the feet dilates capillaries before oil application.)

Blend 1 ml (15 to 20 drops) of Celastrus paniculatus seed oil with 9 ml of sesame oil in a small metal bowl and warm gently over a hot water bath for 1 minute. (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: Do not overheat; test a drop on your wrist.)

Massage 5 ml of the warm oil blend into the sole, heel, and Kshipra Marma (web between big toe and second toe) of each foot using circular strokes for 5 minutes per foot. (Duration: ~10 min. Tip: Focus on the center of the arch (Talahridaya Marma).)
Put on old cotton socks to protect bedsheets and lie down immediately for sleep. (Duration: ~1 min. Tip: For external foot massage (Padabhyanga) only.)
storage: Store the blended oil in a closed glass bottle away from sunlight for up to 30 days. (Maximum shelf life: 720 hours).

traditionalUses: Traditionally used for general anxiety, nervous debility, and stress-induced sleeplessness

ingredients.notes: 4 g (approx. 1 level teaspoon coarse churna) — Shade-dried whole aerial herb

ingredients.name: Hot boiled water
ingredients.notes: 150 ml (approx. 1 teacup) — For steeping

ingredients.notes: 30 ml (approx. 2 tablespoons) — Added after straining

ingredients.name: Palm sugar or rock sugar (Panakarkandu / Mishri)

steps: Measure 4 g of dried Evolvulus alsinoides (Vishnukranti) whole-plant coarse powder into a ceramic cup. (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: Ensure the herb was shade-dried rather than sun-bleached.)
Pour 150 ml of freshly boiled water over the herb and cover the cup with a lid. (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: Steeping preserves scopoletin and betaine alkaloids.)
Steep covered for 10 minutes, then strain through a fine muslin cloth. (Duration: ~10 min. Tip: Press the marc lightly.)
Stir in 30 ml of warm cow's milk and 5 g of palm sugar, and sip lukewarm 45 minutes before sleep. (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: Take in a calm evening routine.)

titleEn: Durva / Garike (Cynodon dactylon) & Sandalwood Cooling Forehead Paste (Shirolepa) for Sleeplessness
communityOrTradition: Vokkaliga, Halakki Vokkaliga, Classical Karnataka Ayurveda — Traditional Karnataka ethnomedicinal & Ayurvedic topical forehead paste for Pitta insomnia
traditionalUses: Traditionally used for sleeplessness accompanied by burning eyes, forehead heat, and stress headache

Cooling topical herbal paste (Shirolepa / Pralepa) freshly ground from tender blades of Durva grass (Cynodon dactylon) and white sandalwood (Santalum album) with rose water, applied across the forehead before bedtime to draw out Pitta heat and induce tranquil sleep.

ingredients.name: Fresh tender blades of Cynodon dactylon (Durva grass)
ingredients.notes: 15 g (approx. 1 handful, roots removed) — Washed thoroughly in clean water

ingredients.name: Pure white sandalwood powder (Santalum album)
ingredients.notes: 3 g (approx. 1/2 teaspoon) — Authentic Chandana powder

ingredients.name: Pure distilled rose water (Gulab Jal)
ingredients.notes: 15 ml (approx. 1 tablespoon) — Grinding medium

steps: Wash 15 g of fresh tender Cynodon dactylon (Garike) grass blades thoroughly to remove all soil and chop into 1 cm pieces. (Duration: ~4 min. Tip: Harvest only clean upper green blades.)

Grind the chopped grass on a clean stone slab with 3 g of white sandalwood powder and 15 ml of rose water into a smooth, cool green paste. (Duration: ~5 min. Tip: The paste should be thick enough not to drip into the eyes.)

Lie down comfortably and spread an even 3 mm layer of the cool paste across the forehead and temples (avoiding the eyebrows and eyelids) for 20 minutes. (Duration: ~20 min. Tip: Close your eyes and breathe slowly while the paste cools the forehead.)

Wipe off the paste gently with a damp warm cloth before it dries completely cracks, pat dry, and go to sleep. (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: In Ayurveda, Shirolepa should always be wiped off while still slightly moist.)
storage: Prepare fresh before application; wash off with lukewarm water before falling asleep. (Maximum shelf life: 4 hours).

communityOrTradition: Classical South Indian & Ayurvedic Tradition — Classical South Indian & Ayurvedic Medhya Rasayana drink for nervous irritability and restlessness
traditionalUses: Traditionally used for mental irritability, emotional agitation, nervous exhaustion, and pitta-type sleep disturbance

Refreshing, calming Medhya drink prepared from the freshly extracted juice of mature white ash gourd (Benincasa hispida / Kushmanda) seasoned with a pinch of cardamom and jaggery, taken in the afternoon or early evening to cool Sadhaka Pitta and stabilize mood.

botanicals.plantPart: fresh mature fruit pulp (rind and seeds removed)

ingredients.name: Fresh mature white ash gourd pulp (Benincasa hispida)
ingredients.notes: 150 g (cubed, peel and seeds removed) — Select an ash-coated mature fruit

ingredients.name: Crushed green cardamom seeds (Elettaria cardamomum)
ingredients.notes: 0.5 g (approx. 2 pods) — Balances the cooling potency

ingredients.name: Crushed black pepper (Piper nigrum)
ingredients.notes: 0.5 g (approx. 1 pinch) — Prevents Kapha accumulation

ingredients.name: Unrefined jaggery or rock sugar
ingredients.notes: 5 g (approx. 1 teaspoon) — Classical Anupana

steps: Cut 150 g of mature white ash gourd (Benincasa hispida), trim off the tough green outer rind and central seed pith, and dice the white flesh into cubes. (Duration: ~4 min. Tip: Always use mature ash-dusted Kushmanda rather than immature fruits.)

Grate or blend the 150 g of cubed flesh without adding extra water and squeeze through a clean muslin cloth to obtain approximately 100 ml of fresh juice. (Duration: ~4 min. Tip: Ash gourd is over 90% structured water and yields abundant juice naturally.)

Stir in 0.5 g of crushed cardamom, 0.5 g of black pepper, and 5 g of jaggery until dissolved. (Duration: ~1 min. Tip: Adding a pinch of black pepper and cardamom makes it safe for Vata-Kapha individuals.)
Drink at room temperature in the late afternoon or early evening. (Duration: ~1 min. Tip: Do not add ice.)
storage: Consume freshly pressed at room temperature within 2 hours; never refrigerate. (Maximum shelf life: 2 hours).

traditionalUsage.typicalAdultAmount: 100 ml of fresh seasoned ash gourd juice once daily.
traditionalUsage.typicalFrequency: Once daily for 15 to 30 days
traditionalUsage.traditionalTiming: Late afternoon or early evening on a light stomach

doshaEffect: Strongly pacifies Pitta and Vata; Chetorogahrut (calms mental agitation) and Medhya

redFlagSymptoms: insomnia lasting more than 3 to 4 weeks or causing severe daytime impairment
loud snoring with pauses in breathing or gasping at night (sleep apnea)
severe depression, panic attacks, or thoughts of self-harm
unexplained palpitations, chest pain, or nocturnal breathlessness
stopAndSeeDoctorIf: Consult a qualified physician if sleeplessness persists beyond 3 weeks or is accompanied by severe anxiety, depression, or breathing pauses during sleep.
If you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or taking sedative, anti-epileptic, or blood-pressure medications, ask a clinician before using this preparation.
Do not combine herbal sedatives with prescription sleeping pills or alcohol.

sources.citation: R. Kulkarni, K.J. Girish, A. Kumar (2012). Pharmacological and clinical review on Kushmanda (Benincasa hispida) as a Medhya Rasayana (Kulkarni et al., 2012). Pharmacognosy Reviews.

evidenceNote: Documented in R. Kulkarni, K.J. Girish, A. Kumar (2012), Pharmacognosy Reviews. Refreshing, calming Medhya drink prepared from the freshly extracted juice of mature white ash gourd (Benincasa hispida / Kushmanda) seasoned with a pinch of cardamom and jaggery, taken in the afternoon or early evening to cool Sadhaka Pitta and stabilize mood.

titleEn: Jethimadh / Yashtimadhu (Glycyrrhiza glabra) Licorice Root & Warm Milk for Calming & Sleep
communityOrTradition: Rabari, Charan, Classical Ayurvedic Tradition — Classical Gujarati & Charaka Samhita Medhya Rasayana evening milk for Vata-Pitta restlessness
traditionalUses: Traditionally used for mental fatigue, emotional exhaustion, and vata-pitta insomnia

Naturally sweet, soothing bedtime drink prepared by whisking fine licorice root powder (Glycyrrhiza glabra / Yashtimadhu) into warm cow's milk (exactly as prescribed in Charaka Samhita's Medhya Rasayana quartet) to nourish Ojas, calm the nervous system, and support restful sleep.

ingredients.name: Fine root powder of Glycyrrhiza glabra (Yashtimadhu churna)
ingredients.notes: 3 g (approx. 1/2 level teaspoon) — Sieved fine root powder

ingredients.name: Warm cow's milk
ingredients.notes: 150 ml (approx. 1 teacup) — Classical vehicle specified in Charaka Samhita

ingredients.name: Crushed fennel seeds (Foeniculum vulgare)
ingredients.notes: 1 g (approx. 1/4 teaspoon) — Optional aromatic adjunct

steps: Pour 150 ml of cow's milk and 1 g of crushed fennel seeds into a small saucepan and bring to a gentle simmer for 3 minutes. (Duration: ~4 min. Tip: Do not boil licorice powder directly in milk for long, as high acid/tannin release can curdle milk.)
Remove the milk from the heat, strain out the fennel seeds into a mug, and let cool for 1 minute to around 65°C. (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: Warm milk blends smoothly with Yashtimadhu churna.)

Whisk 3 g of fine Glycyrrhiza glabra (Yashtimadhu) root powder thoroughly into the warm milk. (Duration: ~1 min. Tip: No extra sugar is needed as glycyrrhizin is naturally 50 times sweeter than sucrose.)
Sip lukewarm 30 minutes before bedtime. (Duration: ~1 min. Tip: Soothes both the throat and the nervous system.)
storage: Prepare fresh at bedtime and drink warm. (Maximum shelf life: 4 hours).

traditionalUsage.typicalAdultAmount: 150 ml of warm milk mixed with 3 g of Yashtimadhu root powder.
traditionalUsage.typicalFrequency: Once daily at bedtime for 14 to 21 days

doshaEffect: Pacifies Vata and Pitta; Medhya Rasayana, Ojovardhaka, and Manasashantikara

titleEn: Shatapatri / Gulkand (Rosa damascena) Sun-Cured Rose Petal Preserve in Warm Bedtime Milk
communityOrTradition: Kannauj & Awadhi Traditional Unani-Ayurveda — Traditional Awadhi & Kannauj (Uttar Pradesh) cooling floral nightcap for Pitta insomnia
traditionalUses: Traditionally used for pitta-type insomnia, night heartburn, irritability, and disturbed sleep

Aromatic, cooling bedtime milk prepared by stirring sun-cured Damask rose petal preserve (Gulkand of Rosa damascena) and a pinch of crushed fennel into warm cow's milk to cool Sadhaka Pitta, calm emotional heat, and promote sweet, uninterrupted sleep.

ingredients.name: Traditional sun-cured Gulkand (Rosa damascena petals with Mishri)
ingredients.notes: 10 g (approx. 1 level tablespoon) — Prepared from fragrant pink Damask rose petals

ingredients.name: Whole cow's milk
ingredients.notes: 150 ml (approx. 1 teacup) — Heated and slightly cooled

ingredients.name: Green cardamom powder (Elettaria cardamomum)
ingredients.notes: 0.5 g (1 pinch) — Enhances aroma

steps: Bring 150 ml of cow's milk with 0.5 g of green cardamom powder to a gentle boil in a small saucepan. (Duration: ~3 min. Tip: Use a clean steel or enamel pan.)
Remove the milk from the stove and allow it to cool for 2 minutes until warm (about 55°C). (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: Do not boil Gulkand over high heat as it diminishes the rose otto aroma.)
Stir 10 g of sun-cured Gulkand into the warm milk until the rose syrup dissolves and the tender petals infuse. (Duration: ~2 min. Tip: No extra sweetener is needed.)
Drink the warm rose-infused milk and chew the soft petals 30 minutes before sleep. (Duration: ~1 min. Tip: Especially soothing on warm nights or when experiencing nocturnal acidity.)
storage: Serve warm or lukewarm 30 minutes before bedtime. (Maximum shelf life: 4 hours).

traditionalUsage.typicalAdultAmount: 150 ml of warm milk mixed with 10 g of Gulkand at bedtime.
traditionalUsage.typicalFrequency: Once daily at night for 14 to 30 days

doshaEffect: Pacifies Pitta and Vata; Hridya (calms the heart/mind), Dahaprashamana, and Nidrajanana
